PropTrack exposes this through a developer program of REST APIs — covering address suggestion and matching, property and listing data, sold-transaction search (including point-and-radius queries), automated valuations, and market metrics — documented on a hosted Stoplight developer portal and secured with OAuth 2.0. The APIs are aimed at banks, lenders, brokers, proptech platforms, and other enterprise customers integrating Australian property intelligence.

providers.name: Apartments.com
providers.description: Apartments.com is the largest United States rental-listings marketplace, owned by CoStar Group since its 2014 acquisition and operated from Arlington, Virginia as the anchor of the Apartments.com Network — a group of consumer rental sites that also includes ApartmentFinder.com, ApartmentHomeLiving.com, ForRent.com, ForRentUniversity.com, WestsideRentals.com, Apartamentos.com, After55.com and CorporateHousing.com. It sits on the demand side of the US residential value chain as an Internet Listing Service (ILS): apartment owners and property managers buy advertising, and their inventory, availability, pricing, media, concessions and fee data flows in from property management systems (Yardi, RealPage, Entrata, MRI, AppFolio, ResMan, Rent Manager, Funnel, EliseAI and others) rather than from any public API, while leads flow back out to the advertiser's CRM. Its API posture is closed. Apartments.com publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI or OData $metadata contract, no SDK, no webhooks and no Postman collection; developer.apartments.com, developers.apartments.com and docs.apartments.com do not resolve in DNS, and api.apartments.com resolves only to the same Akamai edge that returns HTTP 403 Access Denied to every non-browser request, including robots.txt. The one documented machine-to-machine seam is the Digital Feeds Program — an approval-and-contract path in which an approved third-party feed vendor syndicates a paying advertiser's listings into Apartments.com over FTP using an XML listings feed whose specification guide is available only on request to Feeds@apartments.com. A second inbound seam lets licensed agents opt in to rental-listing syndication through their own MLS (Bright MLS, ARMLS, REcolorado, OneKey MLS, SmartMLS, NorthstarMLS, MLS PIN, Garden State MLS, New Jersey MLS and Aspen Glenwood MLS are documented), which requires MLS membership. On RESO, the honest reading is absence rather than "certified but unreachable": Apartments.com does not appear anywhere in the RESO certificates list, and its own property-manager help centre returns zero results for "RESO". It is a consumer of MLS rental feeds, not a certified RESO endpoint, and no unlicensed open dataset is published.

providers.name: Nuvolo
providers.description: Nuvolo is a modern Integrated Workplace Management System (IWMS) and Enterprise Asset Management provider that delivers its Connected Workplace suite natively on the ServiceNow platform. It unifies facilities and space management, real estate and lease administration, capital planning and projects, maintenance and work management, healthcare technology management (HTM), GxP and life-sciences asset management, refrigeration management, sustainability and energy, and OT security into a single cloud platform. Nuvolo serves healthcare, life sciences, public sector, retail, and education organizations, helping them manage the full lifecycle of their assets, spaces, and facilities with mobile access and real-time reporting. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: RealScout
providers.description: RealScout is a lead-nurture and collaborative home-search platform for real estate professionals — agents, teams, and brokerages — that turns an agent's existing database and local MLS inventory into a recurring source of transactions. It is CRM-agnostic and plugs into existing stacks (Follow Up Boss, Sierra, Salesforce, HubSpot) via native integrations, Zapier/Make, and direct API access on Enterprise plans. Core products include AI Search (natural-language-to-MLS-criteria), Scout Score (0–100 contact engagement scoring), Contact Enrichment, Search Links, and Auto-Nurture alerts. RealScout publishes an OAuth 2.1-protected, standards-compliant MCP server (api://realscout-admin-mcp) for agent/AI access. Backed by DCM Ventures.

providers.name: Better Mortgage
providers.description: Better (Better Home & Finance Company, operating as Better Mortgage) is a New York-based fintech founded in 2014 by Vishal Garg that digitizes home finance end to end. Its online platform originates purchase mortgages, refinances, home equity lines of credit (HELOC), and VA loans, and connects borrowers with title, closing, homeowners insurance (via Better Cover), and real-estate agent matching. Better was the first fintech to fund over $100 billion in home loans entirely online and markets an "AI-powered" One Day Mortgage experience. Better does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, but it operates a live OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 identity provider (backed by AWS Cognito) for partner single sign-on, discoverable at its /.well-known endpoints.

providers.name: Greenlite
providers.description: GreenLite Technologies is a construction permitting and plan-review platform that uses AI-powered technology and expert services to streamline building-permit approval for builders, developers, and jurisdictions. Its products include Atlas (a real-time permit tracking and management dashboard), LiteTable (AI-assisted plan review and code-compliance analysis), Private Plan Review (PPR), and Code Compliance & Pre-Check. GreenLite claims to reduce permitting timelines from 90-120+ days to 21-45 days and serves national QSR, retail, healthcare, education, and financial-institution brands. Backed by Craft Ventures and Insight Partners. GreenLite currently exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its company identity and security posture.

providers.name: AppFolio
providers.description: AppFolio is a Santa Barbara, California cloud-based real estate technology company providing property management software to residential, commercial, community association (HOA), student housing, single-family, and affordable housing operators, plus investment management tooling for sponsors and funds. Its flagship AppFolio Performance Platform unifies workflow automation, accounting and reporting, marketing and leasing, maintenance, resident communication, and resident services on a single multi-tenant SaaS. AppFolio embeds Realm-X, an in-house agentic AI layer (Realm-X Assistant, Performers, Flows) directly into the platform rather than as an add-on. Integrations are delivered through the AppFolio Stack marketplace, where certified partners (ButterflyMX, Conservice, HappyCo, Knock, Lowe's, Property Meld, and many more) connect via the AppFolio Stack API. The Stack API is gated behind a partner application, security-compliance questionnaire, and terms-of-service signing; OAuth 2.0, a sandbox environment, webhooks, and an OpenAPI/Swagger reference are made available only to approved partners through the developer.appfolio.com portal, so no public specification is reachable for catalog inclusion. AppFolio's revenue model is per-unit SaaS subscription plus value-added services (payments, screening, insurance, marketing). The AppFolio GitHub organization publishes internal Ruby on Rails, React, and tooling libraries (react-gears, ae_page_objects, store_base_sti_class) but no public API SDK, CLI, or OpenAPI artifact.

providers.name: Standard Industries
providers.description: Standard Industries is a privately-held global industrial company headquartered in New York City and tracing its origins to 1886. The company operates a portfolio of building solutions, performance materials, logistics, real estate, and investment businesses, with more than 20,000 employees and approximately $11 billion in annual revenues. Standard Building Solutions includes GAF (North America's largest roofing manufacturer), GAF Energy (Timberline Solar nailable solar shingles), BMI Group (Europe's largest pitched and flat roofing manufacturer, with brands including Braas, Monier, Icopal, Wolfin, and Redland), Siplast (specialty roofing and waterproofing for iconic structures), SGI (mining and mineral processing), Schiedel (flue, stove, and ventilation systems), and Standard Logistics. Performance Materials is anchored by W. R. Grace & Co., which produces catalysts, engineered materials, process technologies, and fine chemicals. Standard Investments deploys capital across public equities and early-to-growth venture investments. Winter Properties is a vertically integrated real estate firm with more than 100 years of history in New York City. Standard Industries does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at the corporate level; technology integration with customers and partners is handled inside the individual operating companies (most notably GAF and Grace).

providers.name: CrowdStreet
providers.description: Crowd Street (formerly CrowdStreet) is an online private-markets investing platform that gives accredited investors direct access to commercial real estate, private equity, venture capital, private credit, and real estate fund offerings. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, the company operates a marketplace where sponsors raise capital and members subscribe to individual deals, diversified funds, and managed portfolios, alongside an education center, glossary, and research library. Crowd Street Capital LLC is a FINRA-member broker-dealer and Crowd Street Advisors LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser. The platform is delivered as a members-only investor web application; as of this profile Crowd Street publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: LendingPad
providers.description: LendingPad is a cloud-based mortgage loan origination system (LOS) that lets brokers, lenders, and institutions originate, process, underwrite, close, and fund residential mortgage loans with real-time, multi-user collaboration across the borrower, broker, lender, and service-provider lifecycle. It ships in Broker, Lender, Processing, and Institution editions and runs a large Partners Marketplace of integrated vendors (credit, AUS, AVM/appraisal, title, compliance, doc-prep, pricing/PPE, POS, CRM, and investors such as Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, UWM, and Rocket Mortgage). LendingPad exposes an Enterprise API for loan data exchange, but access is gated - it is limited to Lender Edition clients under an executed API Agreement and NDA, keys and testing-site access are issued by the support desk, and there is no public developer portal or self-serve API reference. The API entries below are honestly modeled from the vendor-integration and marketplace capabilities LendingPad describes publicly; endpoint-level surfaces are not published and are not fabricated here.

providers.name: Pretto
providers.description: Pretto is a French online mortgage brokerage (courtier en credit immobilier) operated by FINSPOT SAS, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Paris. It runs a digital platform that lets borrowers simulate a home loan, compare rates across more than 125 partner banks, assemble a financing file and be accompanied by a human credit expert through to signature, and it publishes a transparent, non-negotiable fee schedule instead of the bank-funded commission model used by most French brokers. Pretto also operates Pretto Galaxie, a B2B network that opens the same technology stack — semi-automated file assembly, an embeddable loan simulator, a client portal, a commission dashboard and a back-office service — to independent brokers, and Pretto Search, a consumer property-search product priced against real borrowing capacity. FINSPOT is registered with ORIAS (17000916) as a banking/payment-services and insurance broker and is supervised by the ACPR. As of this pass Pretto publishes no public developer program: the api.pretto.fr host serves its API reference behind HTTP Basic auth and the developers.pretto.fr ReadMe hub is deactivated.

providers.name: Summer 2
providers.description: SummerOS (formerly reached at gosummer.com, which now 308-redirects to summeros.com) is an AI-driven asset-intelligence platform for short-term rental operators, owners, investors, and property managers. It provides professional-grade revenue forecasting, competitive market intelligence, and portfolio-wide performance analytics, plus an AI assistant (Sunny AI), so short-term rental teams can make data-driven pricing and investment decisions instead of relying on spreadsheets. It connects to property-management systems (Guesty, Hospitable, Streamline, Track) rather than exposing a public developer API. Surfaced as a QED Investors portfolio lead and enriched from its live public surface.

providers.name: Blueground
providers.description: Blueground is a global proptech company that leases, furnishes and operates move-in-ready apartments for stays of a month or longer, running thousands of units across cities in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Latin America. It operates an end-to-end technology stack: a consumer booking site and iOS/Android guest apps, an internal property, pricing and operations platform, and the Blueground Partner Network — an invite-only marketplace where third-party furnished-rental operators list supply and connect inventory through PMS and channel-manager integrations (Avantio, NextPax, Rentals United, Hostify, Hostfully, SiteMinder, Cloudbeds, Airbnb). Blueground publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable contract: partner connectivity is brokered through channel-manager partners rather than a self-serve API. Its engineering organization does maintain a real open-source footprint on GitHub (bluegroundltd), with libraries released to Maven Central and npm, and the main website publishes an llms.txt.

providers.name: Buildium
providers.description: Buildium, part of RealPage, is a cloud property-management platform aimed at small and mid-sized residential, association, and community-association property managers. The platform covers accounting, leasing, applicant and tenant management, rent collection, maintenance, communications, owner and resident portals, and association management. Buildium publishes a Public API used by certified partners and customers for property, lease, tenant, owner, vendor, rental application, financial, and webhook integration with the Buildium platform.

providers.name: Aceable
providers.description: Aceable (Aceable Brands) is an Austin, Texas mobile-first online education company founded in 2013 that builds state-accredited licensing and continuing-education courses across four brands: Aceable (drivers ed, defensive driving and traffic school in 40+ US states), Aceable Agent (real estate pre-license, post-license and CE in 16 states, plus PrepAgent exam prep in all 50), Aceable Insurance (Property & Casualty and Life & Health pre-license in 13 states, CE in CA/IL/TX) and Aceable Mortgage (NMLS-approved MLO pre-license and CE in 7 states plus the required 20-hour national component; NMLS Provider ID 1400102). More than 20 million students have been licensed through Aceable, at roughly 1.5 million per year. The company raised about $106M across five rounds from Silverton Partners, Floodgate, Sageview Capital and HGGC, and operates a B2B partner program (affiliate and bulk-buy) for driving schools, school districts, brokerages, carriers and mortgage employers. Aceable publishes no public developer API or developer portal; its platform API at api.aceable.com is a private, application-ID-gated backend serving the Aceable web and mobile apps.

providers.name: Build
providers.description: Build is an AI-native operating partner for the built world, pairing autonomous AI agents (its "Dougie" platform) with deep domain expertise to accelerate commercial real estate and infrastructure development. The platform automates mission-critical development workflows including site selection, due diligence, underwriting, investment-committee memos, test-fit analysis, market and zoning research, environmental diligence, and ESG reporting. Build serves institutional clients across data centers, industrials, energy, power, office, telecommunications, mixed-use, hotels, and multifamily. Backed by Index Ventures; profiled in the API Evangelist network. Build is a services company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Real Estate Institute of Australia
providers.description: The Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA), founded in 1924 and based in Canberra, is the national federation of the eight state and territory Real Estate Institutes (REINSW, REIV, REIQ, REIWA, REISA, REIT, REIACT, REINT), which between them represent roughly 85% of Australian real estate businesses and agents. REIA is a policy, research and accreditation body, not an operator of market infrastructure: it administers the REIA National Principles of Conduct that underpin state institute codes and training, awards Associate (AREI) and Fellow accreditations, runs the Australasian Auctioneering Championships (AUSTROS) jointly with REINZ and the National Awards for Excellence (NAFE), makes submissions to the Commonwealth Government, and publishes the quarterly Housing Affordability Report (HAR) and Real Estate Market Facts (REMF) series that Federal Treasury, the Reserve Bank, state treasuries and investment banks subscribe to. It sits well above the transaction rail in the Australian value chain - listings run through REA Group's realestate.com.au and Domain, settlement through PEXA, valuation through PropTrack and CoreLogic, and title through the state land registries - and REIA touches none of those pipes. Its API posture is therefore an honest absence: no developer portal, no API subdomain, no OpenAPI or OData contract, and no RESO reference anywhere on its estate, because RESO is a NAR-mandated United States construct with no Australian counterpart. What REIA sells is data, not access to it - the HAR and REMF reports are AUD 450 subscriptions and each of the 7 HAR and 15 REMF underlying datasets is a separate AUD 280 subscription, delivered as documents through a platformOS/Insites ecommerce storefront with Stripe checkout behind an email-and-password account. Policy submissions, standalone research reports and the strategic plan are freely downloadable PDFs; the quarterly numbers are not, and there is no open data.

providers.name: OnTheMarket
providers.description: OnTheMarket is the third-largest residential property portal in the United Kingdom, operating onthemarket.com. It was founded in 2013 by Agents' Mutual Limited as an agent-owned challenger to Rightmove and Zoopla, listed on AIM as OnTheMarket plc, and was acquired outright by CoStar Group in December 2023 for approximately GBP 99 million. In a market with no MLS and no cooperative listing standard, OnTheMarket sits at the demand end of the value chain: consumers search the portal, and listings arrive from member estate agents' CRM systems rather than from a shared data pool. Its API posture is honest and narrow. There is no public developer portal — developer., developers., api. and docs.onthemarket.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs all return 404 on the main site. What does exist is a member-only integration surface: the OnTheMarket Real Time Datafeed (RTDF), a Rightmove-RTDF-compatible feed API served from the live, OnTheMarket-operated host realtime-api.onthemarket.com, used by agency CRM vendors to push listings and pull branch enquiries on behalf of member agents. No machine-readable contract for it is published anywhere; OnTheMarket's developer guide is distributed under agreement, and every path on the host returns 404 to an anonymous caller. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the stack — RESO is a North American construct and the UK has never adopted it, so "certified but unreachable" does not apply here; there is no certification layer in this market at all. OnTheMarket publishes no open data. The genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector — HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey — and none of it comes from the portals. OnTheMarket's own Terms of Use go further than most and expressly forbid automated access to any page other than the home page.

providers.name: Realtyna
providers.description: Realtyna provides real estate technology including IDX, RESO Web API integrations, MLS data routing, and a WordPress-based property platform (WPL). Their API Plugin exposes the WPL platform via a RESTful, JSON-based HTTP interface for building custom front-ends and mobile applications. Realtyna also offers MLS API, Organic RESO API, and the MLS Router API for enterprise MLS integration.

providers.name: Simon Property Group
providers.description: Simon Property Group is the largest retail real estate investment trust (REIT) in the United States, owning, developing, and managing premier shopping, dining, entertainment, and mixed-use destinations. Simon's portfolio includes an interest in 254 properties: traditional malls, premium outlets, Mills centers, lifestyle centers, and other retail properties in North America, Europe, and Asia. The company operates ShopSimon, an e-commerce platform, and Simon Innovation Group to advance retail technology innovation. Simon had trailing twelve-month revenue of approximately $6.36 billion as of 2025 and a market capitalization of approximately $67 billion.

providers.name: VendorPM
providers.description: VendorPM is a PropTech procurement and vendor-lifecycle-management platform for the commercial real estate industry, unifying vendor credentialing, compliance screening, eTendering/eBidding, procurement, and contract management under a single login. Its marketplace connects property managers with a network of 50,000+ vendors to fulfill building services and contracts of all sizes, while an AI Procurement CoPilot surfaces recommendations and a Yardi Voyager ERP integration syncs vendor compliance and profile data. VendorPM serves 100+ property management groups and 6,000+ buildings across the US and Canada. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company; VendorPM exposes no public self-serve developer API — its Yardi/ERP integration is provisioned through a Customer Success Manager.

providers.name: Roofstock
providers.description: Roofstock is a residential real estate investment platform and online marketplace for buying, selling, and managing single-family rental (SFR) homes. It gives individual and institutional investors research, analytics, certified property listings, and end-to-end services spanning acquisitions, property management (Mynd), portfolio accounting software (Stessa), tenant screening (RentPrep), asset management, and dispositions across dozens of U.S. markets. The company reports hundreds of thousands of users and over $10B in transacted volume. Roofstock operates a private web API (api.roofstock.com) and a GraphQL endpoint powering its marketplace applications; it does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, first-party SDKs, or documented API access. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and SoftBank Vision Fund and enriched from Roofstock's public web surface.

providers.name: OLX
providers.description: OLX is a global online classifieds and marketplace operator, part of OLX Group (owned by Prosus / Naspers), running consumer buy-and-sell marketplaces across 30+ countries under 20+ brands including OLX Poland (olx.pl), OLX Brazil (olx.com.br), OLX Portugal, OLX Bulgaria and OLX Romania, spanning general classifieds, motors/autos, and real estate. OLX Poland publishes a public Partner API (OAuth2) that lets integrators and sellers manage adverts, categories/attributes, and delivery settings programmatically. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and General Catalyst and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Northspyre
providers.description: Northspyre is a real estate development management platform that gives owners, developers, and project teams an end-to-end system for managing deals, projects, and portfolios across the full development lifecycle — acquisition, early planning, pre-development, construction, and stabilization. It unifies siloed project data and automates routine work with tools for financial modeling and deal pipeline management, budget and cost control, vendor procurement and management, forecasting, portfolio analytics, and investor and lender reporting. Northspyre is delivered as a hosted SaaS application and is SOC 2 Type II certified. It exposes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity, compliance posture, and domain security.

providers.name: Staircase
providers.description: Staircase, Inc. operates the Elephant Protocol (elephant.xyz), a decentralized property-data network that aggregates and cryptographically verifies fragmented county property and address records into trusted, agent-consumable data. It publishes 500,000+ enriched property data points and an unusually agent-native developer surface: a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (@elephant-xyz/mcp, both stdio and hosted), an Elephant CLI (@elephant-xyz/cli) for oracle data transformation and on-chain proof submission to Polygon, a fact-sheet generator, and a library of 14 published Agent Skills for county-data ingestion. An Enterprise API is offered to organizations at scale. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners; originally a mortgage-technology API company, now focused on real estate data infrastructure.

providers.name: Arrived
providers.description: Arrived is a real estate investment platform that lets individuals buy, own, and sell fractional shares of income-producing residential properties without the work of being a landlord. Investors browse curated single-family rentals, vacation rentals, funds, and real-estate debt offerings, invest in minutes, and receive passive rental income through dividend distributions plus potential appreciation while Arrived handles acquisition and property management. The company reports roughly 981K registered investors, $445M invested, and $95M distributed. Arrived is a consumer-facing investing product with a web and mobile app; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Storefront
providers.description: Storefront (thestorefront.com) is an online marketplace for renting short-term commercial retail space, connecting brands, e-commerce businesses, and artists with space owners to launch pop-up shops, showrooms, galleries, product launches, and events. The platform lists tens of thousands of spaces across 50+ cities in North America, Europe, and Asia, with flexible day/week/month rentals and a secure booking-and-payment flow, 24-hour support, and a Priority Pass membership. Storefront was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal (api.thestorefront.com is private/401), so this profile captures company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Honeyhomes
providers.description: Honey Homes is a home-maintenance membership service that pairs each member with a dedicated, vetted handyman who handles repairs, upgrades, seasonal upkeep, and preventive maintenance around the house. Members book visits, add tasks, receive photo updates, and stay connected to their handyman and team through a companion mobile app. Founded in 2021 by Vishwas and Avantika Prabhakara and backed by Khosla Ventures, the company operates as a licensed, bonded, and insured General Contractor and serves select California and Texas markets including the San Francisco Bay Area and Dallas. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company; the company exposes a consumer mobile app but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: PermitFlow
providers.description: PermitFlow is an AI-powered construction permitting platform that simplifies permit preparation, submission, and tracking nationwide for contractors, home builders, commercial contractors, architects, developers, and home-services businesses. The product handles permitting paperwork across municipalities with AI agents for intake, research, submission, coordination, and issuance, and covers permit management, inspections and closeouts, and license and registration management. Backed by Accel, Felicis, and Initialized Capital, PermitFlow operates an internal product API (api.permitflow.com) and web application (app.permitflow.com) but does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Royal LePage
providers.description: Royal LePage is Canada's largest residential real estate brokerage brand, founded in Toronto in 1913 as A.E. LePage and operated today under franchise and corporately-owned brokerages by Bridgemarq Real Estate Services (TSX: BRE), an affiliate of Brookfield. It spans roughly 20,000 licensed REALTORS across 600-plus offices nationwide, and sits in the value chain as a brokerage/franchisor rather than as a data platform. Its consumer search at royallepage.ca is a downstream CONSUMER of listing data, not a publisher of it - the site states its inventory is "226,755 active MLS listings via the CREA DDF network," meaning the machine-readable feed belongs to the Canadian Real Estate Association's Data Distribution Facility, not to Royal LePage. On API posture the honest finding is that there is none published for developers - no developer portal, no documented API, no OpenAPI or OData $metadata, no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification anywhere in evidence (RESO is a US NAR-adjacent regime and is simply absent from the Canadian brokerage layer), and no SDKs, webhooks, or Postman collections. Account registration on the site creates a Virtual Office Website (VOW) relationship with Royal LePage Real Estate Services, Brokerage that restricts data to personal, non-commercial use, and the legal notice expressly forbids "spiders, robots, crawlers, data mining tools, or the like." Any programmatic access to the underlying Canadian listing record runs through CREA membership and the DDF licence, not through Royal LePage.

providers.name: Rentals.ca
providers.description: Rentals.ca is a Toronto-headquartered residential rental marketplace and the flagship brand of the Rentals.ca Network, which also operates Rentfaster.ca, Louer.ca, Rentboard.ca, RentCanada.com and TorontoRentals.com across more than 100 Canadian cities. The network is owned and operated by Rentsync (formerly Landlord Web Solutions Inc.), which also acquired the research firm Urbanation in January 2026 and co-publishes the monthly Rentals.ca / Urbanation National Rent Report; Rentals.ca listing data also feeds a Statistics Canada rental housing index. In the Canadian real estate value chain it sits on the rentals side of the market, outside CREA's REALTOR.ca and Data Distribution Facility, which syndicate member boards' for-sale listings. Its API posture is honest but closed: rentals.ca itself publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI, and no documented public endpoint, and the entire consumer site sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that returns HTTP 403 to anonymous clients. The real developer surface belongs to the parent, at the Rentsync Partners portal (partners.rentsync.ca, branded "LIFT System API"), which publicly names a REST API, an Ad Syndication API and a Search API but places all documentation behind an account whose registration form requires a written application explaining what you intend to build. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document, no Universal Property Identifier, and no open dataset published by the company.

providers.name: GoPillar
providers.description: GoPillar (operated by CoContest Italy Srl, Rome, Italy) is a crowdsourced architectural and interior design marketplace where homeowners, businesses, and small construction firms launch online design contests and receive dozens of proposals from a global community of 70,000+ registered architects and designers. Clients set a project timeline, brief the community, message participating designers, and select the winning concept, with follow-on one-to-one and offline executive-project services. GoPillar also runs GoPillar Academy, an e-learning platform offering professional BIM, 3D, and design courses plus custom corporate training for architecture and construction firms. GoPillar is a consumer/SMB web platform and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public web identity and domain security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: HostnFly
providers.description: HostnFly is a French short-term-rental (Airbnb) concierge and property-management company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Paris. It manages the full lifecycle of short-stay rentals on behalf of property owners: listing creation and optimization, multi-platform distribution (Airbnb, Booking.com, Abritel), guest screening and 24/7 communication, check-in/check-out and key handling, hotel-grade housekeeping and linen, maintenance, short-term-rental insurance, and dynamic revenue optimization. HostnFly operates on a commission-only model (from ~20% of nightly revenue, no fixed fees) and covers 340+ cities across metropolitan France and Corsica. It is a Partech portfolio company. HostnFly publishes an llms.txt agent-discovery file but does not expose a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Milo Credit
providers.description: Milo (formerly Milo Credit) is a Miami-based financial technology company and licensed mortgage lender that pioneered crypto-backed lending. Milo lets cryptocurrency holders access cash or finance U.S. real estate without selling their digital assets, offering crypto-backed mortgages with up to 100% financing, self-custody mortgages, and crypto-backed loans funded in as little as 24 hours, with rates starting around 7%. The company was an early portfolio investment of QED Investors and operates as a consumer-facing lending platform rather than a developer/API-first company. As of this enrichment pass Milo publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; its public surface is a consumer web application (app.milo.io), a marketing site, a blog, an FAQ, and a hosted trust/security center. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Vennre
providers.description: Vennre is a Sharia-compliant private-market investing platform built for HENRYs (High Earners, Not Rich Yet). It curates and vets institutional-grade opportunities across real estate, private equity, venture capital and private credit from leading global managers, lowering entry thresholds so members can start building wealth from as little as $5,000. Delivered through a mobile app and web experience with a smart wallet, portfolio tracking and personalized wealth coaching, the platform is regulated in the UK as an appointed representative of Talbot Capital Ltd (FCA FRN 489839) and operates in Saudi Arabia under the Capital Market Authority (CMA License 19206-20). Vennre is a consumer wealthtech product; no public developer API or developer platform is published at this time.

providers.name: Lastro
providers.description: Lastro is a Brazilian proptech company building artificial intelligence for the real estate market. Its product, Lais (lais.ai), is a generative-AI platform for real estate agencies that engages and qualifies inbound leads over WhatsApp and other channels, then follows the customer journey from first contact through to a closed deal — covering property listing and management, marketing and lead generation, pre-qualification, visit scheduling, administrative service and strategic reporting. Human agents and the AI work the same queue inside Casa da Lais, the operator dashboard. Lastro reports more than 1,000 real estate agency customers, over 5 million people served and more than R$ 12 billion in sales volume (VGV) managed in Brazil. The company is backed by Prosus Ventures and QED Investors. Lastro publishes no public developer API; the only programmatic surface found is the Wix platform-provisioned site MCP endpoint on lastro.co.

providers.name: Wayhome
providers.description: Wayhome (formerly Unmortgage) is a London-based property technology company founded in 2016 by Nigel Purves and Josef Wasinski. It offers "Gradual Homeownership" — a part-buy, part-rent alternative to a traditional mortgage in which a customer buys at least 5% of a home and pays rent on the remainder, gradually increasing their ownership stake over time. Wayhome pairs aspiring homeowners with institutional investors (including Allianz), letting people who can afford rent but cannot secure a conventional mortgage move into a home of their choice with a deposit as low as 5%. Wayhome is authorised and regulated in the United Kingdom. It is backed by fintech venture investors including Anthemis, Augmentum Fintech, Allianz X and Accelerated Digital Ventures. Wayhome operates as a consumer-facing service and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: Boxabl
providers.description: BOXABL Inc. is a Las Vegas, Nevada manufacturer of factory-built, foldable homes, founded in 2017 and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker BXBL. Its homes are assembled on a production line in a climate-controlled factory rather than on site, then folded to 8.5 by 20 feet for shipment by truck, rail, sea or air and unfolded on the pad in about two hours. The Casita is the current production model, sold as a studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom in unit-only or turnkey configurations, with a Baby Box travel trailer and a multi-unit Developer Series catalog alongside it. BOXABL publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; its machine-readable surface is an agent-facing llms.txt, a permissive AI-crawler robots.txt, and an RFC 9116 security.txt pointing at a real responsible-disclosure and bug bounty policy.

providers.name: Brookfield Asset Management
providers.description: Brookfield Asset Management (NYSE: BAM, TSX: BAM) is a leading global alternative asset manager with over $1 trillion in assets under management and approximately $614 billion in fee-bearing capital. BAM describes itself as "a pure-play, asset-light investment manager with earnings derived from stable, predictable fee-related revenue." The publicly listed manager was formed in December 2022 when it was spun out of Brookfield Corporation (NYSE: BN), which remains the majority shareholder. BAM operates across five investment verticals — Renewable Power & Transition, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Private Equity, and Credit — and adjacent Insurance Solutions capability is delivered through Brookfield Wealth Solutions, a sister business within the broader Brookfield ecosystem. BAM does not publish a public developer API program. Institutional Limited Partners, financial intermediaries, distribution platforms, and portfolio companies interact with the firm through private, authentication-gated investor portals, PDF reporting (10-K, supplemental, letters to shareholders), data feeds from fund administrators, and the investor-relations website at bam.brookfield.com.

providers.name: Limehome
providers.description: Limehome is a Munich-headquartered digital hospitality operator founded in 2018 that designs, leases and runs fully-equipped design apartments and aparthotels across Europe, from Berlin to Barcelona and Linz to Lecce. The company runs a 100% digital guest journey: guests browse and book units online, receive an access code, and complete check-in and check-out contactlessly with no on-site reception staff. Limehome operates offices in Munich and Madrid with more than 200 employees, is led by CEOs Dr. Josef Vollmayr and Cesar de Sousa Freitas, and is backed by Picus Capital, HV Capital and Lakestar. Revenue comes from direct bookings (fee-free, with a 15% membership discount) alongside a "Lease to Limehome" real-estate partnership model. Limehome runs a production API host at api.limehome.com behind AWS API Gateway, but publishes no public developer portal, documentation or machine-readable specification; that surface is first-party/private. The company does maintain a public GitHub organization with a small number of open-source engineering libraries, and an engineering blog.

providers.name: Property Capsule
providers.description: Property Capsule (PropertyCapsule) is a retail and commercial real estate marketing automation and prospecting platform for landlords and brokers. It centralizes property, tenant, and availability data in one place and automatically publishes it as flyers, tourbooks, interactive site plans, aerials, demographics, and competition maps across web and iPad leasing apps. Founded around 2014, the company was acquired by VTS in October 2019 and its capabilities were folded into the VTS Market product. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures.

providers.name: Arrived Homes
providers.description: Arrived (Arrived Homes) is an SEC-qualified real estate investing platform that lets anyone buy fractional shares of income-producing single-family rental homes and vacation rentals for as little as $100. Arrived curates and acquires properties nationwide, handles acquisition, financing, property management, tenant placement, maintenance, and financial reporting, and passes rental income to investors as quarterly dividends alongside long-term appreciation. The platform also offers pooled funds including a Single Family Residential Fund and a Real Estate Income (debt) Fund. As of profiling it reports roughly 981K registered investors, $445M invested, and $95M distributed. Backed by Forerunner Ventures, it operates as a consumer fintech / proptech product with a web and mobile app; it publishes no public developer API. This API Evangelist profile is enriched from public company surfaces.

providers.name: Peerspace
providers.description: Peerspace is an online marketplace for booking unique venues and spaces by the hour — event spaces, meeting rooms, photo and film studios, production locations, and unconventional rooms and residences — connecting space owners (hosts) with people who need distinctive locations for events, meetings, photo shoots, and productions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network. Peerspace operates a consumer marketplace with web and mobile apps but does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and legal and support surface.

providers.name: Lennar
providers.description: Lennar Corporation is a Fortune 500 company and one of the leading homebuilders of new homes for sale in the United States. Lennar operates an internal Azure-hosted API Management developer portal where Lennar developers and partners discover and consume Lennar Corporation APIs. Public OpenAPI artifacts have not been observed; access generally requires sign-in and partner approval.

providers.name: Expansive
providers.description: Expansive is a Mexican real estate crowdfunding platform (crowdfunding inmobiliario) that lets individuals invest collectively in vetted real estate projects from as little as 1,000 MXN, earning returns backed by real guarantees. It operates as a regulated collective financing institution (IFC) under Mexico's Fintech Law and is supervised by the CNBV (Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores). Expansive handles project vetting, funding, quarterly investor reporting, and payouts through its web platform and investor app (app.expansive.mx). The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing fintech investing product; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: PreFix
providers.description: PreFix is a Techstars-backed residential home-maintenance service company operating in Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, and Denver. For a flat monthly membership, homeowners get a dedicated neighborhood Home Manager who handles general repairs, twice-yearly 30-point preventive maintenance, HVAC, plumbing, carpentry, painting, appliance and garage-door work, and vetted contractor management through a single email, call, or text. Customers manage their homes through the HomeHub member portal. PreFix operates a consumer home-services business and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and demand-side intelligence.

providers.name: Cape Analytics
providers.description: Cape Analytics (now part of Moody's) is a geospatial property intelligence provider that applies computer vision and machine learning to high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery, property records, and other novel data sources to produce inspection-quality condition and characteristic data for over 100 million residential and commercial structures across the United States and Canada. Its insights — roof condition and material, swimming pools, solar panels, accessory structures, tree overhang, wildfire and wind exposure, distance to hazards, and a proprietary Liquidity Score — are delivered to insurance underwriters, lenders, and real estate investors in under two seconds via API, batch/bulk files, an Automated Property Condition Report (aPCR), and a customer web portal, as well as through third-party platforms such as Guidewire and Duck Creek. Cape does not publish a public, self-service developer portal or open API specification; API access is provisioned to customers and partners through a gated onboarding flow.

providers.name: Housewhisper
providers.description: HouseWhisper (legal name Real Estate Productivity, Inc.) is a Seattle-based AI platform for real estate teams and brokerages, founded by former Zillow executives. It acts as a 24/7 AI teammate that automates the full lead lifecycle through personalized voice and text conversations: a Lead Engine that re-engages and revives cold database contacts, a Rules Engine that routes leads to the right agent with fallback escalations, and an AI Teammate that handles CRM updates, follow-ups, scheduling, reminders, and administrative busywork by call or text. It connects to real estate CRM, dialer, and calendar systems via API keys with no data migration, integrating with Follow Up Boss, Sierra Interactive, kvCORE, MoxiWorks, Salesforce, Lofty, HubSpot, and others. Pricing is outcome-based (a small monthly platform fee plus referral fees on closed deals). HouseWhisper has raised roughly $10M in seed funding led by Mayfield. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Lamudi
providers.description: Lamudi is an online real estate classifieds marketplace focused exclusively on emerging markets, founded in 2013 and today operating consumer property portals in the Philippines (lamudi.com.ph), Indonesia (lamudi.co.id) and Mexico (lamudi.com.mx). The platform lets buyers, renters, sellers and landlords search and list houses, condominiums/apartments, land, commercial space and offices, filtered by geography, property group and operation (buy/rent). Search results pages carry area market statistics, interactive maps and nearby points of interest, alongside country-specific features such as Philippine foreclosures and home-loan comparison, Indonesian KPR mortgage simulators, and Mexican Infonavit-eligible listings and bank repossessions. Agencies and developers publish inventory through the pro.lamudi.com professional portal. Lamudi operates as part of LIFULL Connect, which supplies its legal notice, privacy policy and contact surface. Lamudi publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal; its notable machine-readable surface is a first-party llms.txt on each country site that documents the URL grammar of its search, new development and project pages for AI agents.

providers.name: Lessen
providers.description: Lessen is a Scottsdale, Arizona based property services and facilities management technology company that connects commercial and residential property owners and managers with a nationwide network of vetted service providers for repairs, maintenance, turns, make-readies and capital projects. The company operates a technology platform stack — One by Lessen for work-order, vendor-sourcing and invoicing workflow, Lessen 360 for multifamily maintenance, Lessen Pro for affiliate contractors, Aiden for AI-assisted work-order creation, and the Lessen Marketplace for procurement — supported by mobile apps for tenants, property managers and vendors. Lessen serves retail, financial services, healthcare, food service, industrial, hospitality and education properties alongside single-family and multifamily residential portfolios. Lessen acquired SMS Assist in 2023 and is backed by Fifth Wall and General Catalyst. Lessen publishes no public developer portal, API reference or OpenAPI definition; its named platform integrations are delivered as private partner connections rather than a self-serve API program.

providers.name: Trelora
providers.description: Trelora is a technology-driven, full-service discount real estate brokerage founded in Denver, Colorado and now operating as part of HomeSmart. It lets people buy and sell homes for a low, transparent fee instead of the traditional percentage-based commission, helping sellers save thousands of dollars and offering buyers cash-back rebates of up to several thousand dollars at closing. Trelora pairs salaried, non-commissioned real estate agents with an online platform and IDX-powered property search across markets including Colorado, Washington, and other U.S. states, and publishes a real estate blog, glossary, and city-level market reports. Originally a Techstars-backed startup, Trelora is consumer-facing and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Haven Connect
providers.description: Haven Connect is an affordable-housing software company (founded 2014, San Jose, CA) that streamlines the affordable-housing application and waitlist process for both property managers and low-income applicants. Its web platform lets property managers publish waitlists, collect and screen online applications, and automate waitlist updates — eliminating paper forms and manual data entry — while giving applicants a single portal to find and apply for affordable housing. Haven Connect is a Techstars Impact portfolio company and has raised roughly $2.9M. It is a SaaS product company with no public developer API; this profile captures its public website, support, and commercial surfaces for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Acretrader
providers.description: AcreTrader is a farmland investment platform headquartered in Fayetteville, Arkansas that lets accredited investors buy fractional, passive ownership stakes in individual US row-crop, permanent-crop and timberland farms. AcreTrader sources and vets each farm, then handles the legal entity, farm management and administration while investors earn returns from annual cash rent and long-term land appreciation. Securities are offered through North Capital Private Securities Corporation, a FINRA/SIPC member broker-dealer that is not an affiliate of the platform. Since 2018 AcreTrader has enabled investment in over 140 farmland properties spanning roughly 44,000 acres across 20 states, and its investment management arm, AcreTrader Management LLC, reports net IRR of 9.4% to 30.3% on realized deals. Proterra Investment Partners LP acquired AcreTrader in August 2025. AcreTrader publishes no public developer API, no developer portal and no machine-readable specification; contract discovery was run in full against acretrader.com and api.acretrader.com on 2026-08-10 and every discovery path returned 404.

providers.name: Houm
providers.description: Houm (Houm Technologies SpA) is a Chilean proptech operating a digital real-estate brokerage and rental-management marketplace across Chile, Mexico and Colombia, with operations in Santiago, Viña del Mar, Concepcion, Bogota and Ciudad de Mexico. Founded in 2018 by Benjamin Labra and Nicolas Knockaert, the company lets owners list, rent and sell apartments and houses without a guarantor (sin aval), guarantees on-time rent payment to the owner even when the tenant does not pay, and runs a network of freelance field agents ("Houmers") who photograph, show and manage properties. Its ReV pricing algorithm (houm.com/cl/algoritmo-precio) values a property online, and it also runs an investor product and a broker exchange (Houm Aliados / Canje Corredores). Houm raised a $35M Series A in 2021 led by Goodwater Capital. As of this profile Houm publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; its production backend at api.houm.com answers 403 to every anonymous request and carries no published documentation.

providers.name: HomeLight
providers.description: HomeLight is a San Francisco–based real-estate technology company that matches home buyers and sellers with top-performing local real-estate agents and operates a stack of consumer-facing products that span the entire residential transaction: agent matching, Simple Sale cash-offer marketplace, Buy Before You Sell (BBYS) bridge financing, HomeLight Home Loans (NMLS #1529229), the HomeLight HELOC Card, and HomeLight Closing Services for title and escrow. The company ranks agents using historical performance data on home sales (price, speed, volume, geography, property type) and routes consumer leads to a curated network of agents, lenders, and cash-buyer investors. HomeLight exposes a private Partner API to lenders, brokerages, CRMs, and marketing partners (NerdWallet is its largest partner) for submitting leads (`/api/partner_lead/v2`), Simple Sale seller leads (`/leads/partner_simple_sale_lead`), and duplicate-lead checks (`/api/partner_dupe_lead_check`); credentials are issued on a per-partner basis via support@homelight.com. Beyond the Partner API, HomeLight has direct integrations with most major real-estate agent CRMs (Follow Up Boss, BoomTown, Sierra Interactive, Firepoint, Real Geeks, Brivity, Chime, LionDesk, KW Command). HomeLight has no public, self-service developer portal — the Partner API is gated by a commercial relationship, and there is no public OpenAPI spec, SDK, or open-source client published by the company.

providers.name: LeaseLock
providers.description: LeaseLock is an insurtech platform for rental housing that replaces the traditional cash security deposit with lease insurance. Its Zero Deposit program embeds coverage into the lease through a signed addendum, removing thousands of dollars of move-in cost for residents while protecting owners and operators against unpaid rent and damage. LeaseLock Shield applies AI to ledger data, market trends and lease profiles to underwrite risk, and LeaseLock Central gives property teams a portal for claims, support tickets and training. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Dallas, Texas, the company says it integrates with all major property management systems, but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, API reference or client SDKs — integration is arranged as a managed engagement. Its public engineering output is two open-source PostgreSQL extensions, pgasync and pgflow.

providers.name: Letswork
providers.description: Letswork is a Dubai-headquartered flexible workspace booking platform that lets members work from coworking spaces, cafes, hotels, meeting rooms, private offices and creative studios through a single credit-based monthly membership with no long-term contract. Founded in 2019 by Omar AlMheiri and Hamza Khan, the platform covers 1030+ workspaces across 63+ cities in 18+ countries, serving 80,000+ members across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa. The product ships as iOS, Android and web apps with one-tap check-in, day passes, hourly meeting-room booking, a private-offices marketplace, and team plans that add a shared credit pool, admin dashboard and usage analytics for hybrid companies. Letswork publishes no public developer API or developer portal; it does publish a first-party llms.txt canonical fact set for AI assistants.

providers.name: Renew Financial
providers.description: Renew Financial (Renew Financial Group LLC) is a specialty consumer finance company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Oakland, California that pioneered and administers Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) financing for residential energy efficiency, renewable energy, water efficiency and resiliency home improvements. It administers the CaliforniaFIRST program in California and RenewPACE in Florida, funding solar, HVAC, roofing, windows, landscaping, hurricane and seismic projects through a voluntary property tax assessment repaid over terms up to 30 years. The company is licensed by the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation as a PACE Program Administrator (#60DBO-90653) and carries NMLS ID 1788120. Renew Financial runs a contractor technology platform and an online homeowner application, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Worq
providers.description: WORQ is Malaysia's largest community-centric coworking space operator, backed by 500 Global, offering private offices, dedicated desks, hot desks, virtual offices, meeting rooms, event spaces, and day passes across twelve locations in Greater Kuala Lumpur and Selangor. WORQ publishes no public developer portal or API as of July 2026.

providers.name: Belong Home
providers.description: Belong is a residential property management platform and rental marketplace that helps homeowners rent out their homes and helps residents find and live in professionally managed homes. Marketed as "Property Management Made Loveable," Belong pairs AI-driven pricing and operations with a human care team to deliver guaranteed rent, resident screening and placement, listing distribution across 26+ sites (Zillow, Apartments.com, and more), 24/7 maintenance via a network of Pros, rent collection, and financial tools for both homeowners and renters. The company operates across a growing set of US markets including the SF Bay Area, Seattle, Arizona, Florida, and the East Coast, and is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. Belong is a consumer and homeowner-facing product; no public developer API, SDK, or machine documentation surface has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Block Renovation
providers.description: Block Renovation is a home renovation and construction platform that connects homeowners with vetted, local contractors and provides free design, cost-estimation, and project-planning tools for kitchen and bathroom remodels, home additions, basement renovations, ADUs, new construction, and commercial projects. It operates across all 50 US states and layers on a protection program covering price assurance, progress-based payments, a workmanship warranty, and dedicated Project Planner support. Backed by Obvious Ventures and the SoftBank Vision Fund, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; as of this enrichment pass Block Renovation publishes a consumer-facing marketplace but no public developer API, documentation, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Ergeon
providers.description: Ergeon is a nationwide outdoor residential construction company that installs fencing (wood, vinyl, metal, and chain-link), artificial grass, wooden decks, and concrete driveways, patios, and walkways. It pairs a distributed workforce with technology — live video estimates, a 3D fence-quoting calculator at fencequoting.com, satellite site-plan tooling, and a customer portal — to deliver fast, accurate quotes plus managed installation with permit handling, financing (Wisetack), and workmanship warranties. Ergeon runs internal software and vendor integrations (Stripe, Twilio, Talkdesk, AWS, Lob) but does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, status, and open-source surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GoWork
providers.description: GoWork is Indonesia's largest premium coworking and flexible office space provider, operating more than 25 locations across Jakarta, Tangerang, Surabaya, Bali, and Medan. Formed from the 2018 merger of GoWork and Rework, the company offers private offices, dedicated desks, coworking memberships, virtual offices, meeting and event spaces, plus podcast and live-streaming studios. It also bundles business services such as company incorporation, tax and accounting, visa and work-permit processing, and legal support. Members discover, book, and manage workspace through the GoWork mobile apps and web booking platform. GoWork is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Hubble
providers.description: Hubble (hubblehq.com) is the UK's largest flexible-workspace marketplace, connecting businesses with private offices, coworking desks, day offices, meeting rooms, and on-demand workspace across thousands of buildings in the UK and beyond. Founded in 2014 by Tushar Agarwal and Tom Watson, the platform lets companies configure, deliver, and manage all their space in one place on flexible one-to-24-plus-month terms, and was acquired by Yardi in January 2025. Hubble runs a consumer-facing web platform and internal backend API rather than a published public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web, security, and discovery surface.

providers.name: Piinpoint
providers.description: PiinPoint is an AI-powered location intelligence and site selection platform for retailers, restaurants, brokers, and commercial real estate teams. The software combines demographic, mobile-location, traffic, and competitive data to help teams validate sites, forecast sales, model cannibalization, run network simulations, and plan expansion. Delivered as a B2B SaaS web application (app.piinpoint.com), PiinPoint does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Safqah Holdings Limited
providers.description: Safqah Holdings Limited operates Safqah (Safqah Capital / Safqah Financial), a Saudi Arabian fintech platform headquartered in the Al-Malqa district of Riyadh and regulated by the Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA). Safqah provides Sharia-compliant, debt-based real estate investment opportunities that let qualified individual and institutional investors fund real estate development deals starting from 1,000 SAR, alongside a financing arm that offers land acquisition, residential development, commercial development, raw land, and bridge financing to real estate developers. Investors track deal performance through periodic reporting and live project camera feeds. The platform is a consumer- and investor-facing web application with no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or integration surface at this time.

providers.name: WiredScore
providers.description: WiredScore is the global standard-setting organization for digital connectivity and smart technology in the built environment. It assesses, benchmarks, and certifies buildings through two programs — WiredScore (digital connectivity) and SmartScore (smart building technology) — across office, residential, industrial, and hotel asset types. Landlords, developers, and occupiers in more than 40 countries use its certifications and its network of Accredited Professionals to demonstrate that a building meets modern technology and connectivity expectations; over 4,000 buildings covering roughly one billion square feet have been certified. WiredScore is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Fifth Wall. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Spectora
providers.description: Spectora is home inspection software used by more than 10,000 inspectors to build inspection reports, schedule jobs, manage clients and agents, run a website, take payments, and automate follow-up. Spectora does NOT publish a public, self-serve developer REST API and there is no developer portal, API reference, or API keys for third-party programmatic access as of this writing. Integration with outside systems is instead delivered three ways: (1) a Zapier integration (requires the paid Spectora Advanced add-on) that fires triggers when agent or client contacts are created or updated; (2) outbound webhooks configured through Advanced Actions that POST event data to a URL you supply (e.g. Zapier, Make, or your own endpoint); and (3) a fixed set of named, vendor-built partner integrations (QuickBooks Online, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Mailchimp, HomeBinder, RecallChek, Repair Pricer, Blipp Reviews, InterNACHI BuyBack, and call-center partners). All of these are configuration-time connectors and one-way (outbound) event flows rather than a documented request/response API you can call.

providers.name: Bruce
providers.description: Bruce is a curated professional intro network for licensed real estate, mortgage, title & escrow, and insurance professionals, built by Tanda Technologies, Inc. and founded by Jesse Chor. Rather than a directory, review site, or CRM, Bruce verifies each member's license and role, then lets them log intros and build a portable, verifiable track record. The Bruce Card is each member's living profile — stats, deals, intros, and market rank — that replaces the resume and the "trust me" claim with a sharable credential. Bruce also runs an AI-hosted editorial publication at blog.bruce.bot that profiles verified members in interview-style stories. Backed by Initialized Capital; surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: CBRE Australia
providers.description: CBRE Australia is the Australian arm of CBRE Group, the global commercial real estate services and investment firm, trading locally as CBRE (Gwsla) Pty Ltd (AU09949) and operating across the Pacific from cbre.com.au. It sits on the advisory and management side of the Australian property value chain rather than the data-infrastructure side: capital markets and investment sales, leasing and occupier advisory, valuation and advisory services, property and asset management, and project and design-and-build delivery across office, retail, industrial and logistics, build-to-rent, and alternative asset classes. Its API posture is closed. As of 26 July 2026 no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable contract, or self-serve onboarding exists for CBRE Australia: developer.cbre.com.au, developers.cbre.com.au, api.cbre.com.au, and docs.cbre.com.au do not resolve, and the global developer.cbre.com host is NXDOMAIN as well. CBRE does run API infrastructure — api.cbre.com sits behind an Imperva WAF that returns 403 to every anonymous request, api-dev.cbre.com serves a default WSO2 API Manager landing page, and eipportal.cbre.com is a login-gated "Integration Platform" SPA — but none of it is published, catalogued, or reachable by an outside developer. Commercial listings are distributed through the cbre.com.au property search and Australia's portal duopoly, and CBRE's terms of use explicitly prohibit scraping property listings from the site. RESO is absent entirely, which is the honest answer for Australia: there is no MLS here, no RESO-certified Australian organization, and the country's mandated machine-readable property rail is PEXA's electronic conveyancing network, not a RESO Web API. Access to CBRE data in Australia is a client or partner relationship, not a developer signup.

providers.name: Hometap
providers.description: Hometap is a Boston-based fintech founded in 2017 that offers homeowners a home equity investment (HEI) — an alternative to home equity loans and HELOCs. In exchange for a share of a home's future value, homeowners receive cash up front with no monthly payments, no interest, and no income or debt-to-income requirements, settling any time within a 10-year term via sale, refinance, or buyout. Homeowners manage their investment and track equity through the free Hometap Home Equity Dashboard. The company has helped more than 26,000 homeowners and completed over $1 billion in investments, and is backed by investors including General Catalyst. Hometap does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its public web properties and identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Zibo
providers.description: Zibo (operating as Azibo) is a financial services and property-management platform for independent landlords and rental property owners. The company offers a free-to-use platform that bundles rent collection, tenant screening, online rental applications, lease agreements and eSignatures, document storage, maintenance and messaging, banking, and rental-property accounting. Azibo monetizes through interest on cash balances, card-transaction fees, paid lease/eSignature and screening products, and renter subscriptions such as credit-boost programs. The product is delivered as a SaaS web application (app.azibo.com) that integrates third-party providers including Stripe, Plaid, TransUnion, Latchel, and signNow; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. Zibo was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

providers.name: Zolo
providers.description: Zolo is one of Canada's largest national residential real estate marketplaces and a licensed brokerage, operating as Zolo Ventures Ltd. with provincial brokerage subsidiaries — Zolo Realty (Ontario), (Alberta), (British Columbia), (Saskatchewan), (Manitoba) and (Quebec) Inc. — plus Zolo Mortgages Ltd. and Zolo Mortgages (Alberta) Ltd., all owned by Questrade Financial Group Inc. Founded in 2012 as a digital-first brokerage and headquartered at 1900-5700 Yonge Street in Toronto, Zolo reports over 10 million monthly visitors, 750+ active REALTORS®, and $1.5B+ in annual transaction volume across British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan and Ontario. It sits in the Canadian challenger layer alongside HouseSigma, Wahi and Properly, below CREA — the single national cooperative that operates REALTOR.ca and the Data Distribution Facility (DDF) that syndicates member boards' listings — competing on listing speed, sold-price visibility and home-value tooling over data the boards and CREA control. Its API posture is closed. There is no developer portal, no API program page, no partner or data-licensing page, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind — no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI or MCP surface. The subdomains api., developer., developers., docs., data. and partners.zolo.ca do not resolve in DNS and have never appeared in Certificate Transparency, and every conventional contract path on www.zolo.ca is answered by a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403, cf-mitigated: challenge) rather than a specification. What Zolo does publish is syndication, not integration: an unauthenticated RSS 2.0 new-listings feed at /rss_new_listings.php, a family of sitemaps.org XML documents, and a site-wide schema.org JSON-LD block carrying organization identity only. Behind the edge it operates an undocumented JSON endpoint at /gallery_map_json.php and two first-party mobile apps (com.ols.zolo) on a private backend. Zolo's own robots.txt declares that RSS feed as a sitemap and a CREA terms-acceptance route at /crea_accept.php, and Section 23 of its Terms of Use is a Virtual Office Website (VOW) clause requiring registration, a bona fide interest in buying or selling, personal non-commercial use only, and an express prohibition on "scraping" (including "screen scraping" and "database scraping"), data mining, redistribution or sublicensing — enforceable directly by CREA, TRREB, ITSO, REBGV, Pillar9 and OREB. Access is licensed, not open. RESO is absent: Zolo is not among the nineteen Canadian organizations RESO lists as members, and no Web API or Data Dictionary certification, OData $metadata document, or Universal Property Identifier (UPI) usage was found. No open, unlicensed dataset is published.

providers.name: Baania
providers.description: Baania (Baania (Thailand) Co., Ltd.) is a Thai proptech and real-estate marketplace that aggregates new and second-hand houses, condos, and townhomes for sale across Thailand. The consumer portal provides property listings, project data, reviews, and price comparison to help home buyers make decisions in one place, and connects them directly with property developers and real-estate agents. Backed by 500 Global. Baania is a consumer-facing web portal; no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Construction Monitor
providers.description: Construction Monitor aggregates building-permit data from county and municipal sources nationwide and resells it as construction leads, contractor intelligence, and historical permit research. Programmatic access is offered through a REST + JSON API backed by Elasticsearch and a weekly data-dump option delivered over secure FTP. Both channels are account-managed; partners receive credentials and a documented endpoint contract directly from Construction Monitor.

providers.name: DoorFeed
providers.description: DoorFeed is a technology-led residential real estate investment platform, founded in 2021 and headquartered in Paris, that helps institutional investors, funds, and family offices source and manage single-family rental portfolios at scale across the UK and France. The platform ingests roughly 150,000 new property listings and over 1,000,000 property images every day, structuring market data, comparable transactions, valuation signals, and energy-performance data into a single acquisition and asset-management workflow that takes investors from market screening to investment decision in minutes. DoorFeed is backed by HV Capital, Seedcamp, and Motive Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline; DoorFeed publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: dwell
providers.description: Dwell is a digital publication and lifestyle brand focused on modern home design, architecture, and interior inspiration, published by Ziff Davis. It offers curated home tours, architectural features, renovation and before/after projects, design photography, real estate listings, shopping guides, and design news, plus a Dwell+ subscription for ad-free access and subscriber exclusives, a shop for furniture and decor, and a "Find a Pro" professional directory. Dwell was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent lead in the API Evangelist network; the public dwell.com property is a consumer media site with no developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so no API artifacts are captured for it.

providers.name: Grotto AI
providers.description: Grotto AI is an AI sales-coaching platform purpose-built for the multifamily apartment leasing industry. Founded by former EvolutionIQ leaders Nick Deveau (CEO) and Ben Epstein (CTO), Grotto delivers real-time call guidance, tour and call coaching, and prospect-lifecycle support across email and text that help leasing agents handle objections, book tours, and convert more leads to recover net operating income and asset value. The platform works alongside multifamily systems such as Entrata, Funnel, and Yardi and is used by operators including Weidner Apartment Homes and Hillpointe. Grotto is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27701 certified and Fair Housing compliant. It is backed by ICONIQ. Grotto does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; it is a demo-led enterprise SaaS product.

providers.name: Shweproperty
providers.description: Shweproperty (ShweProperty.com) is Myanmar's leading online real estate marketplace, founded in 2015, connecting buyers, renters, sellers, and agents across the country. The consumer-facing portal lists residential and commercial properties for sale and rent — apartments, condos, houses, land, shops, offices, and industrial zones — in Yangon, Mandalay, Naypyidaw, and beyond, alongside new-development project listings, home-loan assistance with Myanmar banking partners, property events and expos, and real estate news and buyer guides. The platform carries over 200,000 listings with 500+ added daily and handles tens of thousands of monthly sales inquiries. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this remains a consumer web and mobile property portal.

providers.name: Yardi Propware
providers.description: Yardi Propware was the original flagship property management software by Yardi Systems, first released in 1984. It was an early desktop-based real estate management platform for residential and commercial property accounting, leasing, and management. Yardi has since evolved its platform into cloud-based offerings including Yardi Voyager and Yardi Breeze. No publicly accessible developer portal or documented REST API has been confirmed for Yardi Propware specifically; Yardi's modern integrations are managed through the Yardi Interface Partnership Program.

providers.name: Abodu
providers.description: Abodu designs, manufactures, and installs prefabricated accessory dwelling units (ADUs) and backyard homes across California. It offers state-approved plans with fixed all-in pricing and installation as fast as one day, spanning seven models from the 385 sq ft Abodu Studio to the 1,195 sq ft Abodu Three+, plus an Abodu Office. The homes target homeowners seeking rental income, aging-in-place, home offices, and guest houses, as well as multifamily operators, and feature fire-resistant construction with an optional Net Zero solar package. Abodu is a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Aino World Inc.
providers.description: Aino World Inc. builds Aino, an AI-powered spatial analytics platform for architecture, urban planning, and real estate development teams. Aino automates site research by pulling zoning, parcel, transit, demographic, and environmental data from 10+ sources (Google Maps, Regrid, Rentcast, OpenStreetMap, Overture Maps, Microsoft Planetary Computer, Kontur.io, and the US Census), runs GIS-free spatial analysis, and generates presentation-ready maps and dashboards inside a shared, collaborative workspace.
