There is no public Stessa REST API, no developer portal, no SDKs, and no published webhooks; the Stessa community has open feature requests for a public API to pull reports and transactions, but none has shipped.

providers.name: Estateguru
providers.description: Estateguru is a pan-European property-backed crowdfunding and P2P lending platform headquartered in Tallinn, Estonia. Founded in 2013, it connects retail and institutional investors with short-to-medium-term business loans secured by registered mortgages on real estate, operating across Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Finland, Germany, Spain and Portugal. The platform has facilitated over EUR 935 million in funding for 150,000+ investors from more than 100 countries and holds an EU ECSPR crowdservice-provider licence. Estateguru operates as a consumer investment product through its website and iOS/Android mobile apps; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or agent surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of Speedinvest and enriched with its genuinely published company link properties.

providers.name: Inhabit
providers.description: Inhabit is a global PropTech software company operating a portfolio of specialized platforms for the residential and vacation rental property management markets, including ResMan, Streamline, LiveRez, Anyone Home, ResidentIQ, ePremium, Rental Guardian, Lynnbrook Group payments, Western Reporting screening, and Bluetent marketing. Its integrated tools span property management, resident and guest CRM and contact center, payments processing, renters and property insurance, tenant screening and income verification, utility billing, and marketing websites, serving multifamily, single-family, student, affordable, HOA and condo, and short-term vacation rental operators worldwide. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Roam
providers.description: Roam (withroam.com) is a nationwide assumable-mortgage marketplace that helps homebuyers and sellers transact on homes carrying low-rate, legally assumable FHA and VA loans. A qualified buyer can take over a seller's existing mortgage, inheriting the original interest rate, remaining balance, and terms, which in a 6%+ market against sellers' 2-3% loans can save buyers hundreds of thousands in interest. Roam manages the end-to-end assumption process from buyer qualification and lender coordination through paperwork and a 45-day close, and offers proprietary secondary financing so buyers can put as little as 5% down. It is a proptech company backed by Fifth Wall and IVP. Roam publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and llms.txt surface.

providers.name: Beazer Homes USA
providers.description: Beazer Homes USA, Inc. (NYSE: BZH) is an Atlanta, Georgia-headquartered national homebuilder founded in 1985 and publicly listed since 1994. The company designs, sells, and builds single-family and multi-family homes across approximately thirteen U.S. states under brand differentiators such as Choice Plans (customizable floorplans), Mortgage Choice (competitive lender program), Style Choice (interior personalization), and Livable Features (accessibility options). Beazer markets itself as "America's #1 Energy-Efficient Homebuilder," citing homes that are 44% more efficient than the average HERS-rated new home and shipping whole-house ERV ventilation in 100% of homes. As of the most recent public data point (FY2016 10-K), Beazer reported revenue of $1.822B, delivered 5,419 homes, operated 161 active communities, and employed approximately 1,100 people. The company has no public developer program or external APIs; its digital surface is a consumer-facing marketing/community-finder website plus an investor relations portal.

providers.name: Flat
providers.description: Flat (now operating as Clau) is a Mexican proptech real-estate marketplace and financial-services platform backed by 500 Global and Anthemis. Clau lets people buy and rent apartments and houses across major Mexican cities including Mexico City, Guadalajara, Monterrey, and Queretaro, and originates mortgage credit (Cofinavit, construction, land-purchase, and liquidity loans). It also offers property valuations, a price-map database, renovation services, and seller listing tools, alongside "El Living", its real-estate education blog. The company is consumer-facing and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile was surfaced from the 500 Global and Anthemis portfolios and enriched with domain-security and identity signals.

providers.name: Baletu
providers.description: Baletu (巴乐兔) is a landlord-direct online residential rental platform operated by Shanghai Wanjian Information Technology Co., Ltd. Founded in 2012 and based in Shanghai, it lets tenants rent apartments directly from landlords with monthly-payment ("月付") options, reducing agency fees. The platform spans first-tier Chinese cities including Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen plus more than ten second-tier cities, listing over one million properties. Baletu is a consumer proptech company backed by DCM Ventures, Tiantu Capital, Nan Fung Group, and ZWC Partners, having raised roughly $140M through a 2018 Series C. It ships consumer iOS/Android apps and a partner portal; it does not publish a public developer API program (api.baletu.com serves its own apps).

providers.name: FazWaz
providers.description: FazWaz is a Thailand-based property technology company operating one of the most comprehensive real estate portals in Southeast Asia. Through fazwaz.com it aggregates residential and investment property listings — condos, houses, villas, and land for sale and rent — connecting buyers, sellers, renters, and agents across Thailand and neighboring markets, and pairs the consumer marketplace with agent tools, market data, and property-management services. FazWaz is backed by 500 Global. It runs an internal application API and a GraphQL endpoint that power its own web and mobile clients (both disallowed to crawlers in robots.txt); no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal has been published at this time.

providers.name: Culdesac
providers.description: Culdesac is a post-car real estate development company building walkable, car-free neighborhoods in the United States. Its first project, Culdesac Tempe in Tempe, Arizona, broke ground in 2019 and welcomed its first residents in 2021 — a 16-acre, roughly $140 million development of 636 apartment units plus 24,000 square feet of restaurant and retail space, designed with no resident parking. Residents receive transportation benefits such as free light-rail rides and discounted rideshare and scooter access in place of car ownership. Culdesac operates leasing, tours, and resident services through its website and HubSpot-backed portals, and intends to replicate the car-free neighborhood model in other cities. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Culdesac publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: McGrath
providers.description: McGrath is one of Australia's largest residential real estate brokerage networks, founded in Sydney in 1988 by John McGrath and operating a mixed company-owned and franchise network of roughly 118 offices across New South Wales, Queensland, the ACT, Victoria and Tasmania. Its business lines span residential sales, property management and rentals, projects and new-development marketing, rural and livestock, an Asia Desk for offshore buyers, and mortgage broking through Oxygen Home Loans. Listed on the ASX in 2015 as McGrath Limited (ASX:MEA), it was acquired in June 2024 by a consortium of Knight Frank Australia and New Zealand's Bayleys for A$95.5m and delisted from the ASX on 28 June 2024. McGrath sits on the demand side of the Australian property value chain: it is a brokerage that publishes listings into the REA Group (realestate.com.au) and Domain portal duopoly, settles transactions over the PEXA electronic conveyancing network, and consumes valuation data from PropTrack and CoreLogic rather than producing any of those rails itself. Its API posture is honestly nil. No developer portal exists — developer., developers., api., docs., feeds., data. and portal. subdomains of mcgrath.com.au all fail to resolve (NXDOMAIN), and /developers, /api, /docs, /api-docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /$metadata and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return HTTP 404. RESO — the only genuinely mandated machine-readable real estate contract anywhere in this study — is a North American standard driven by NAR and MLS membership; it has no Australian counterpart and McGrath has no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData surface, and no Universal Property Identifier usage. The only interoperability standards McGrath demonstrably implements are robots.txt and twelve XML sitemaps; every /.well-known/ document probed — security.txt, openid-configuration, oauth-authorization-server, api-catalog, ai-plugin.json — and /llms.txt return 404. Its robots.txt enumerates twenty crawler groups including GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot and Bytespider, but under RFC 9309 group-matching rules those named AI agents are disallowed only from Google Maps JS/RPC paths — the /properties/ and /search/ disallow lands solely on User-agent: *, so the listing corpus is nominally open to the named AI crawlers and closed to generic ones, while the properties-buy/sold/rent/leased sitemaps advertise those same URLs. Reachability is the harder gate: www.mcgrath.com.au sits behind a Vercel Security Checkpoint that answers scripted clients with HTTP 429 and a browser challenge on every path, so no unattended agent can read the site regardless of robots.txt. The listing inventory is a marketing asset routed to portals under commercial agreements, not a developer surface.

providers.name: Quantierra
providers.description: Quantierra (Quantierra Advisors LLC) is a quantitative real estate advisory firm that uses proprietary software to source, analyze, and execute real estate transactions on behalf of institutional investors, family offices, nonprofits, and everyone in between. The firm blends data-driven deal sourcing and quantitative underwriting with traditional brokerage and advisory services. Quantierra keeps a deliberately low public profile at the preference of its clients and does not publish a public developer program, API, or self-service platform; its technology is used internally to support client engagements rather than exposed as a product.

providers.name: AVO
providers.description: Avo (avonow.com) was a New York City-based "building commerce" and workplace-amenity platform, founded 2017-2018 out of Y Combinator (S18) and backed by Insight Partners and Kleiner Perkins with roughly $84M raised. It offered white-labeled same-day delivery of groceries, household goods, alcohol and personal-care items into residential and office buildings with no order minimums or delivery fees, plus on-site and virtual event programming and corporate gifting and recognition services, serving apartment communities, corporations, hospitals and universities across New York, New Jersey, Chicago and Houston. Avo published no API, SDK or developer portal, and as of a 2026-07-20 probe its domain resolves to a parked lander with no operational hosts; Y Combinator lists the company as inactive.

providers.name: Getagent
providers.description: GetAgent is a UK PropTech company operating getagent.co.uk, a consumer-facing service that helps home sellers compare and choose estate agents based on independent performance data such as sold prices, time-to-sell, and fees. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Seedcamp, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. No public developer portal, API, or specification surface was discoverable at the time of this pass; the production site is served behind a bot-protection checkpoint, so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Host Hotels & Resorts
providers.description: Host Hotels & Resorts is a leading lodging real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns luxury and upper-upscale hotels operating under premium brands in major U.S. and international markets. No public APIs are offered.

providers.name: Knotel
providers.description: Knotel is a flexible workspace and managed office provider that designs, builds, and operates tailored office space for companies across a global network of locations including Amsterdam, Austin, Berlin, London, Miami, and Paris (through its Deskeo partner). Its business is organized around managed office experiences, member work clubs such as Wyncatcher and Old Sessions House, and a services arm covering design and delivery, fit-out, furniture, amenity and hospitality, workplace strategy, technology and AV, catering, and day-to-day workplace operations. Knotel also works directly with brokers and with building owners who want space leased and operated on their behalf. Knotel is a real estate services business and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; its member-facing mobile app is a white-labeled deployment of the Spacebring coworking platform. The one machine-readable surface it does publish is an llms.txt describing its site for AI agents, alongside a robots.txt that explicitly permits the major AI crawlers.

providers.name: Sekra
providers.description: Sekra is a residential and community development company building spaces designed around human connection — its tagline is "the future of home is Human," with an emphasis on community, culture, and longevity. Sekra partners with property owners, developers, and investors globally to create residential communities, and is expanding to new cities. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Fifth Wall (proptech). As of enrichment, Sekra publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical integration surface — this profile captures its identity and a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Service Properties Trust
providers.description: Service Properties Trust (NASDAQ: SVC) is a real estate investment trust (REIT) with approximately $9.9 billion invested across two asset categories: service-focused retail net lease properties and hotels. As of March 31, 2026 SVC owned 761 net lease properties (over 13.6 million sq ft) and 93 hotels (over 21,000 guest rooms) throughout the United States. The company is externally managed by The RMR Group (NASDAQ: RMR). SVC does not operate a public developer program and exposes no public APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or webhooks; investor-facing endpoints are limited to SEC filings, press releases, email alerts, and end-of-day stock quotes.

providers.name: Tishman Speyer
providers.description: Tishman Speyer is a privately held, global real estate developer, operator, and investment manager founded in 1978 by Robert Tishman and Jerry Speyer and headquartered at 45 Rockefeller Plaza in New York City. The firm acquires, develops, operates, and manages first-class office, residential, retail, industrial, mixed-use, and life-science properties across roughly 40 global markets in the Americas, Europe, and Asia. Its signature portfolio includes Rockefeller Center and the MetLife Building in New York, the MesseTurm in Frankfurt, The Spiral at Hudson Yards, and Mission Rock in San Francisco. Tishman Speyer also operates the Zo tenant-experience program, the Studio flex-workplace platform, the Breakthrough Properties life-science joint venture with Bellco Capital, and the TS Ventures proptech investment arm. The firm has reported approximately $65 billion in assets under management and approximately 3,000 employees. Tishman Speyer does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or open-source repositories; all engagement is handled through corporate, investor, leasing, and tenant-app channels.

providers.name: United Dwelling
providers.description: United Dwelling was a Los Angeles-based real estate development company founded in 2018 by venture capitalist Steven Dietz to address the affordable housing shortage by converting underused garages and backyards into accessory dwelling units (ADUs). The company offered studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom zero-net-carbon units ranging from 328 to 647 square feet and handled permitting, construction, financing, and property management end to end. It raised a $10 million Series B in May 2020 led by Alpha Edison with participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners. The business appears to have wound down - its website has lapsed (Squarespace account expired) and its Los Angeles location is marked closed as of mid-2026 - and it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: CubeSmart
providers.description: CubeSmart (NYSE CUBE) is a self-administered and self-managed real estate investment trust (REIT) and the third-largest owner and operator of self-storage properties in the United States. As of December 31, 2024 the company owns 631 self-storage properties across 25 states and Washington DC, containing approximately 45.8 million rentable square feet, and operates a third-party management platform that pushes the total managed network well past 1,300 properties. Headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, CubeSmart originated as U-Store-It Trust (founded July 2004, IPO October 2004) and rebranded to CubeSmart on September 14, 2011. The company is a component of the S&P 400. CubeSmart does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal — its public technology footprint is limited to the consumer cubesmart.com booking/account site and the CubeSmart mobile apps for iOS and Android.

providers.name: Healthpeak Properties
providers.description: Healthpeak Properties (NYSE: DOC) is an S&P 500 healthcare real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns, operates, and develops real estate for healthcare discovery and outpatient care — concentrated in lab/life-sciences, outpatient medical, and continuing care retirement community (CCRC) senior housing segments. The company tagline is "Where Discovery and Outpatient Care Thrive." Originally founded as HCP Inc. in 1985, the company rebranded to Healthpeak Properties in 2019. On March 1, 2024, Healthpeak completed an all-stock merger of equals with Physicians Realty Trust, combining two of the largest outpatient medical real estate platforms in the United States and adopting the new NYSE ticker DOC (previously PEAK). Healthpeak's portfolio spans roughly 700 properties nationwide, with lab concentrations in the South San Francisco, Boston, and San Diego clusters (including Torrey Pines Science Park and The Cove at Oyster Point) and outpatient medical assets clustered on or near top-ranked hospital campuses such as Medical City Dallas. The company reports that approximately 150,000 scientists, researchers, physicians, and healthcare professionals work in its buildings. As a healthcare REIT, Healthpeak does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or technical integration surface. Its public digital footprint is limited to corporate marketing, an investor relations site, SEC filings, ESG/sustainability reporting, and a press room. Tenant-facing operational systems (work orders, building access, energy reporting) are not exposed externally.

providers.name: Properly
providers.description: Properly was a Toronto-based Canadian digital real estate brokerage founded in 2018 that began as one of the country's only iBuyers — making algorithmic cash offers on Calgary homes — before pivoting to Sale Assurance, a guaranteed-purchase backstop that let a seller buy their next home before selling the current one, wrapped around an online listing search and a machine-generated home valuation. It sat in the challenger layer of the Canadian value chain alongside HouseSigma, Wahi, and Zolo, competing on visibility into listing data controlled by CREA, the national cooperative that operates REALTOR.ca and the Data Distribution Facility (DDF) syndicating member boards' listings, in a market where land registration is provincially privatised and the public record is itself a commercial product. Properly was acquired by Pine Canada Financial Corporation in October 2023 and the brand has since been absorbed: properly.ca and www.properly.ca now answer HTTP 301 from an Amazon S3 and CloudFront redirect bucket to www.pine.ca, and the word "Properly" no longer appears anywhere on the surviving Pine real estate pages. Its API posture is closed and, as of this profile, non-existent. No developer portal, no API program page, no partner or data licensing page, and no published terms of API use were found. The developer., developers., api., docs., app., and blog. subdomains of properly.ca do not resolve in DNS, and every contract path probed — /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs, /$metadata, /odata — redirects into a Pine 404. The successor host api.pine.ca resolves to an AWS API Gateway that answers every path with HTTP 403 MissingAuthenticationTokenException: a private first-party backend, not a developer product. RESO is absent, which is the honest Canadian answer — Properly and Pine appear nowhere on RESO's own Canadian membership roster, and no Web API or Data Dictionary certification, OData $metadata document, or Universal Property Identifier usage was observed. No open, unlicensed dataset is published. The underlying listings reach the platform through licensed channels — CREA MLS trademark attribution appears in the site footer and listing media is served from cdn.repliers.io, the CDN of the licensed MLS data vendor Repliers, whose own developer guide names "Pine (formerly Properly)" as a customer — which is a brokerage and vendor licensing posture, not anything a third-party developer can sign up for.

providers.name: Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust (PREIT)
providers.description: Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust (PREIT) is a Philadelphia-based mall REIT founded in 1960 by Sylvan M. Cohen. The trust developed, owned, and managed mixed-use retail destinations — including Cherry Hill Mall, Woodland Mall, Mall at Prince George's, and Springfield Town Center — across roughly nine states in the eastern and midwestern United States. PREIT filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection twice in four years. The first filing, on November 1, 2020, was a pre-packaged restructuring resolved by December 11, 2020. The second filing, on December 10, 2023, was a more consequential restructuring that wiped out public shareholders. PREIT emerged from its second Chapter 11 in early 2024 as a private company owned by its former lenders (reported to include Redwood Capital Management and Nut Tree Capital Management). Common shares were delisted from the New York Stock Exchange, and Jared Chupaila was appointed CEO of the reorganized, privately held entity. The post-emergence PREIT continues to operate its mall portfolio as a private operator. It exposes no public APIs, no developer portal, no documented machine-readable surfaces, and maintains no GitHub organization. This profile is preserved primarily to document the company's Chapter 11 history and its absence from the API economy.

providers.name: Public Storage
providers.description: Public Storage is an American real estate investment trust (REIT) that acquires, develops, owns, and operates self-storage facilities throughout the United States and Europe. Headquartered in Glendale, California, it is one of the largest self-storage operators in the world, serving customers via its online reservation system (eRental), mobile apps, and physical facilities. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Related Companies
providers.description: Related Companies is a privately held, fully integrated real estate firm founded by Stephen Ross in 1972 as an affordable-housing developer and now active across luxury residential, affordable housing, retail, office, hospitality, data centers, and city-scale mixed-use development. Related is the developer of Hudson Yards in New York City, The Grand LA, Time Warner Center (now Deutsche Bank Center), The 78 in Chicago, and operates regional platforms including Related Beal, Related Midwest, Related California, Related Ross, and Related Argent in the UK. The firm owns and manages roughly 55,000 affordable and workforce housing units and has stated it has never converted a single affordable unit to market rate. Stephen Ross also owns a majority stake in Equinox Holdings (Equinox fitness clubs, Equinox Hotels, SoulCycle, Blink Fitness) and the Miami Dolphins / Hard Rock Stadium.

providers.name: Toll Brothers
providers.description: Toll Brothers is the nation's leading builder of luxury homes, designing, building, marketing, and arranging financing for luxury residential communities across the United States. As a Fortune 500 company and #1 Most Admired Home Builder in Fortune magazine's 2026 list, Toll Brothers operates across 60+ markets. The company does not publicly expose developer APIs. Website integrations and home search functionality are provided through the tollbrothers.com consumer platform.

providers.name: Factory OS
providers.description: Factory OS (styled Factory_OS) is an off-site construction company founded in 2017 by Rick Holliday and Larry Pace that industrialized multifamily and affordable housing production on an assembly line inside a 275,000-square-foot facility in Building 680 on Mare Island in Vallejo, California. Union carpenters build wood-frame housing modules across roughly two dozen stations in a 33-step process, and the finished modules are trucked to the project site and assembled — an approach the company says cuts production time by about half and production cost by a quarter against conventional site-built construction. It raised roughly $132 million across three rounds, including $60 million from JPMorgan Chase and Saint-Gobain in 2021, and delivered more than 4,000 homes across California and Hawaii, about 90 percent of them affordable housing. In May 2024 the company was recapitalized and renamed Harbinger Homes (legal entity Harbinger Production Inc.), with Tom Smith as CEO and Kevin Brown as president; factoryos.com now 301-redirects every path to harbinger.homes. Harbinger filed a WARN notice on 12 February 2026 covering all 280 employees, citing a lack of new business and loss of capital funding, with layoffs beginning 13 April 2026. Factory OS is a manufacturer of physical housing modules, not a software company: it operates no developer program, API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its GitHub organization has no public repositories.

providers.name: Getground
providers.description: GetGround is a London-based property investment platform that lets UK and international buy-to-let investors set up and run their rental businesses through a limited company. The all-in-one platform handles limited company formation, business bank accounts, accounting and tax filing (including Making Tax Digital), bookkeeping, buy-to-let mortgages, landlord insurance, tenant finding, and sourcing of investment properties. GetGround is backed by QED Investors and offers subscription tiers and launch packs for landlords managing single or multiple rental properties.

providers.name: Placester
providers.description: Placester is a real estate marketing and technology platform that provides IDX-enabled websites, CRM, lead generation, and marketing automation tools for real estate agents, teams, and brokerages. Historically Placester published a developer-facing Real Estate API (api.placester.com) for listings, contacts, and website content, but the developer portal (developer.placester.com) now redirects to a site-unavailable page, indicating the public developer program is discontinued or inaccessible. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no accessible public API surface, OpenAPI, or SDK was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: SmartRent
providers.description: SmartRent, Inc. (NYSE: SMRT), founded in 2017 and headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a leading provider of smart home and smart property technology for the multifamily and single-family rental industries. Its platform pairs smart hardware — smart locks, thermostats, water/leak sensors, access control and hubs (Alloy, Fusion) — with cloud-based SaaS for property operators to manage connected devices at scale. Products span smart apartments, building and common-area access control, asset protection and leak monitoring, parking management, self-guided tours, Virtual Intercom (browser-based WebRTC entry), and community/resident WiFi. SmartRent exposes a partner-gated REST API and a Phoenix Sockets real-time API for integrations, but publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI; API credentials are provisioned on request via api@smartrent.com. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: View
providers.description: View, Inc. is a smart-glass and smart-building technology company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Milpitas, California, with manufacturing in Olive Branch, Mississippi. View makes View Dynamic Glass, electrochromic architectural windows whose tint adjusts automatically to sunlight, glare, and heat, alongside a connected Smart Building Platform in which each pane is individually IP-addressable and app-controllable and layered with sensors and services such as SmartProtect (an Azure IoT integration that alerts building managers when glass breaks). Backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund, View went public via SPAC in 2021 and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2024, transitioning back to private ownership under its lenders. View exposes no public developer API surface; its GitHub organization (viewinc) mirrors third-party C/C++ and IoT firmware libraries used internally rather than first-party SDKs.

providers.name: Compass
providers.description: Compass is a leading real estate technology company headquartered in New York City that provides a tech-enabled brokerage platform connecting agents, buyers, and sellers across the United States. The company combines residential real estate services with proprietary software for agents, including marketing, client management, and listing tools. Compass does not currently publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: Purpose Green
providers.description: Purpose Green is a Berlin-based sustainability consulting firm and 360-degree provider for sustainable real estate development, serving property owners and investors who manage multi-unit residential and commercial buildings. The company combines energy auditing (its Energy Light Report tool), ESG reporting, subsidy and grant consultation, renovation project management, and a web-based portfolio management portal (Green+ Portal) to help reduce a building's final energy demand by up to 80%. It is backed by Speedinvest and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company publishes web tools and a customer portal but no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: PennyMac Financial Services
providers.description: PennyMac Financial Services, Inc. is a specialty financial services firm focused on the production and servicing of U.S. residential mortgage loans. The company is one of the largest mortgage lenders and servicers in the United States, providing financing to homebuyers and refinancing to existing homeowners. PennyMac operates through correspondent, consumer direct, and broker channels.

providers.name: 2nd Address
providers.description: 2nd Address (formerly Homesuite) was a Palo Alto, California online marketplace for monthly furnished rentals and corporate housing aimed at business travelers, relocating professionals, and corporate clients. Founded in 2014 and launched in 2015 as Homesuite, it rebranded to 2nd Address in November 2017. Operating as a licensed real estate broker, it listed thousands of furnished homes for extended, month-to-month stays across major U.S. cities, positioning itself against vacation- rental platforms by focusing on longer corporate stays. It raised venture funding from Battery Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, Foundation Capital, and Google Ventures. The company never published a public API or developer program, and its website (2ndaddress.com) is no longer operational, so this profile is an identity record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: 42Floors
providers.description: 42Floors was a commercial real estate (CRE) search engine that made it easy to search for office space, coworking, and commercial listings across major U.S. markets. Founded in 2011 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2012 batch, it was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors and grew a nationwide catalog of hundreds of thousands of listings. The company was acquired by flexible-office provider Knotel in July 2018, and later by real estate software company Yardi in 2021, which folded the 42Floors listing service into its CommercialEdge network of marketplaces (CommercialCafe, CommercialSearch, Point2, PropertyShark). 42Floors no longer operates as an independent brand: its 42floors.com domain now redirects to commercialcafe.com, and it exposes no public developer program, API, or documentation. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio-company lead with no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Acre Homes
providers.description: Acre Homes is a North Carolina-based homeownership company whose mission is to "create the best way to experience homeownership." Acre enables individuals to buy quality homes in desirable neighborhoods while sharing in ownership appreciation and reducing costs, notably without requiring traditional debt financing. Positioned in the wealth and asset management corner of fintech and proptech, the company reframes owning a home as a less financially burdensome decision than the conventional mortgage path, letting residents build equity through a shared-appreciation model rather than a conventional debt-financed purchase. Acre Homes is an early-stage venture-backed company and a portfolio company of Anthemis Group. It operates a consumer-facing homeownership offering and does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or developer documentation; this profile captures verified company identity and public links.

providers.name: Aikito
providers.description: Aikito is a New York-based company (founded 2021) operating a commercial real-estate platform that helps business owners design, build, finance, and manage their commercial spaces. It pairs a suite of AI-driven tools with non-dilutive financing so tenants can build out a space and pay over time, covering the project lifecycle from lease execution through move-in. Aikito was founded by Amol Sarva and its investors include Bloomberg Beta, Gaingels, Calm Ventures, FJ Labs, and Northzone. As of this profile Aikito publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface, so it remains a company/identity record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

providers.name: AquaShield
providers.description: AquaShield is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26 batch) startup building AI-driven water leak detection for buildings and large real estate portfolios. Non-invasive sensors clamp onto existing pipes in minutes with no pipe cutting, retrofits, or downtime; the platform learns each building's normal water-flow patterns and flags anomalies in real time before they escalate into costly damage. Water damage is the largest preventable loss in real estate — more than fire and theft combined. Founded by former MIT and Harvard/EPFL robotics researchers Paul Beckers (CEO) and Marguerite Benoist (CTO), the company is based in San Francisco and works with some of the largest residential portfolios in the world. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; AquaShield currently publishes a marketing site only and does not yet expose a public API or developer program.

providers.name: CalAtlantic Group
providers.description: CalAtlantic Group was a U.S. homebuilder formed on October 1, 2015 through the merger of Standard Pacific Homes and Ryland Homes. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, it became the fourth largest homebuilder in the United States before being acquired by Lennar Corporation in February 2018, which made Lennar the nation's largest homebuilder. CalAtlantic no longer operates as an independent entity and does not offer public APIs or developer resources.

providers.name: Casai
providers.description: Casai was a technology-enabled short-term and furnished-apartment rental company operating across Latin America (notably Mexico and Brazil), surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The enrichment pass found no active developer surface for this entity. The casai.com domain now hosts an unrelated luxury villa rental business (Premium Holiday Rentals and Villas, curated by TravelAI), and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or public API is published under the original company. With no spec-bearing surface, no downstream enrichment artifacts (packages, well-known, MCP, scopes, errors, conformance, etc.) could be produced without fabrication, so this profile remains an identity-only lead.

providers.name: Circa Labs
providers.description: Circa Labs (Circa) was a fintech and proptech startup that operated a rental wealth platform helping renters build financial assets and accelerate their wealth. Backed by Techstars, Circa has since merged with Stake to continue its mission of accelerating renter wealth, and the wearecirca.com site now points to the combined company. No public API, developer platform, SDKs, or developer documentation are published by Circa Labs at this time.

providers.name: Comfy *
providers.description: Comfy (comfyapp.com) was a workplace-experience platform built by Building Robotics Inc. that let employees control lighting, temperature, room booking and office navigation from a mobile app, surfaced here as a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio lead. During enrichment the domain comfyapp.com was found to permanently 301-redirect to Enlighted Inc. / Building Robotics Inc., a Siemens Company, where the product has been rebranded as Siemens Building X space and workplace management; the Enlighted/Comfy site further states operations are ramping down. No independent public API, OpenAPI, SDK, developer portal, well-known discovery surface, or security.txt was found for Comfy or its successor as of this pass. This profile is retained as an acquired/defunct stub with domain-security probe data.

providers.name: Contactually
providers.description: Contactually was a cloud-based CRM (customer relationship management) platform focused on helping real estate agents, brokers, and other relationship-driven professionals nurture their networks through follow-up reminders, contact bucketing, pipelines, and automated outreach. Founded around 2011, it was acquired by real estate brokerage Compass on February 27, 2019, and had already been powering Compass's own CRM. Contactually permanently ceased operations on March 31, 2022. It historically exposed a v2 REST API (api.contactually.com) documented at developers.contactually.com for contacts, buckets, notes, tasks, and webhooks, but that developer surface, the API hosts, and all SDKs are now offline. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct provider; no live API, documentation, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Cover
providers.description: Cover (Cover Technologies Inc.) is a Los Angeles-based construction technology company that designs and builds custom, architect-grade backyard homes, accessory dwelling units (ADUs), and residential spaces using a prefabricated, factory-manufactured building system. Cover handles the full development process end to end, from initial consultation and design through permitting, manufacturing, and on-site installation, delivering custom spaces in weeks rather than years. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of General Catalyst. Cover is a physical-product homebuilder and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures verifiable company identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Creator Cabins
providers.description: Creator Cabins (operating as Cabin, at cabin.city) is a crypto-web3 community project that built globally distributed, coliving neighborhoods uniting members through shared culture, economy, and token-based governance via the Cabin DAO. It began in 2020 with a 28-acre Texas Hill Country property known as Neighborhood Zero and grew into a multi-property network for remote workers before members voted to wind down the formal DAO structure in 2025; individual neighborhoods continue operating independently, and a related Neighborhood Village Project now serves over 100 communities globally. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Elmawkaa
providers.description: Elmawkaa (الموقع) is an Egyptian B2B online marketplace that digitizes construction-materials procurement. Founded in Cairo in 2017 by Ebrahem Anwar, Mahmoud Habib, and Mohamed Thabet, the platform lets construction companies request and compare competitive supplier quotations for materials such as cement, steel, and gypsum board, using proprietary matching algorithms to replace slow, manual bidding with a documented, automated process. A 500 Startups (500 Global) accelerator graduate that raised a seed round led by Flat6Labs with Oqal and other regional backers, Elmawkaa was fully acquired by Saudi PropTech / real-estate-appraisal platform Ayen in a seven-figure deal in October 2024, with its marketplace folded into Ayen's services. Elmawkaa publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation, and its standalone domain (elmawkaa.com) no longer resolves following the acquisition.

providers.name: General Growth Properties
providers.description: General Growth Properties (GGP) was a major U.S.-based commercial real estate company and the second-largest shopping mall operator in the United States before being acquired by Brookfield Property Partners in 2018. The GGP portfolio is now operated under Brookfield Properties. No public developer APIs are documented for the legacy GGP entity.

providers.name: GLP
providers.description: GLP is a leading global logistics real estate and investment management company, developing and operating warehouses, distribution centers, and supply-chain infrastructure alongside a large fund and asset-management business. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of hillhouse and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Sector: logistics. As of this enrichment pass GLP publishes a WAF-protected corporate website but no discoverable public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal; this profile remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Homeboodle
providers.description: Homeboodle was a San Francisco rental marketplace startup that rebranded as "Lovely" around 2012. The product let renters search, apply for, and pay for apartments online, while giving landlords and property managers tools to list units, screen applicants, and collect rent. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) among other investors, Lovely (livelovely.com) was acquired by RentPath (the owner of Apartment Guide and Rent.com) for roughly $13M in April 2014. The company is now defunct as an independent product; livelovely.com issues a 301 redirect to apartmentguide.com and the former developer/API surface (hub.livelovely.com) is offline. This record is retained for historical and network-graph completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Homigo
providers.description: Homigo was a Toronto-based home-services startup, founded in 2016, that later rebranded to Setter and operated a concierge platform giving each homeowner a dedicated concierge to manage home maintenance and repairs — plumbing, HVAC, electrical, landscaping, roofing, pools, masonry, appliances, and handyman work — at the touch of a button. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Thumbtack in December 2020. Its website (setter.com) no longer resolves, and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation were ever published, so there is no live provider surface to enrich.

providers.name: Howard
providers.description: Howard was the world's first flex-use real estate platform, co-founded by Michael Jaindl (CEO) and Derek Lee, aiming to bring flexibility to commercial real estate. It was an early-stage (seed) company backed by Bloomberg Beta out of its 2016 fund. The company has since permanently closed and operates no public developer surface, API, documentation, or live host. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio record and is not an active API provider.

providers.name: Kanler
providers.description: Kanler was a Redwood City, California home-improvement marketplace and construction technology company that connected homeowners with vetted home-improvement professionals and managed their projects end to end, positioning itself around price transparency and project peace of mind. Seed-funded in 2016 with backing from Battery Ventures, Floodgate Fund, TriplePoint Capital and Flight VC, the company later operated as a custom-home and whole-house remodeling firm. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (kanler.com) returns HTTP 404 and no public developer, API, or documentation surface could be found, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Katerra
providers.description: Katerra was a Menlo Park, California off-site construction and building-technology company founded in 2015 by former Flextronics chief executive Michael Marks with Fritz Wolff and Jim Davidson, built on the thesis that a single vertically integrated firm could design, engineer, manufacture and assemble buildings end to end — running its own architecture practice, factories in Phoenix, Tracy and Spokane producing cross-laminated timber and prefabricated wall, floor and bathroom assemblies, and its own supply chain and general contracting arm. It raised more than $2 billion across a dozen rounds, including an $865M Series D led by the SoftBank Vision Fund in January 2018 at a valuation above $3 billion and a $200M recapitalization in December 2020 that handed SoftBank majority control. Its only software product was Katerra Apollo, announced in February 2019 as a design-to-field platform (Apollo Construct, Apollo Insight, Apollo Connect) whose launch materials promised "open API integration" with existing construction workflows — but Apollo was sold to Katerra's own construction customers and never shipped a public developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification. The insolvency of its SoftBank-backed lender Greensill Capital cost Katerra its bonding capacity, and the company shut down and filed Chapter 11 in the Southern District of Texas on 6 June 2021. Its assets were broken up: the Apollo software went to Builders FirstSource for roughly $4.5M on 9 September 2021, and the factories were sold separately. katerra.com no longer serves a site — it answers a Cloudflare error 1001 on every path and cannot complete a TLS handshake at all. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface left to catalog.

providers.name: KB Home
providers.description: KB Home is one of the largest and most recognized homebuilders in the United States, building single-family homes, townhomes, and condominiums for first-time, move-up, and active adult buyers across more than 45 markets.

providers.name: Kodit.io
providers.description: Kodit.io was a Helsinki-based proptech and "iBuyer" that used machine learning and automation to make instant cash offers on residential property, buying homes directly from sellers and reselling them, with operations in Finland, Spain and Poland. Founded in 2017 and backed by Speedinvest among others, the company rebranded to Rive in 2022 after a EUR 23M Series A aimed at simplifying home buying and selling across Europe. In January 2024 Rive (formerly Kodit.io) transferred its entire Finnish real estate brokerage business to Neliöt Liikkuu LKV, and the Kodit.io LKV entity subsequently entered bankruptcy proceedings in late 2024. The company operated a consumer-facing marketplace only; it never published a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts, and the kodit.io domain has since lapsed to an unrelated registrant. This profile is retained as a historical network record.

providers.name: Life House
providers.description: Life House was a vertically integrated hotel software, brand and management company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Miami Beach, Florida. It built its own back-of-house operating system — property management, revenue management, digital marketing and financial operations — for independent hotels, ran more than 50 properties across the United States, Mexico and Canada, and from 2021 sold the platform to third-party hoteliers. It raised over $100M from Inovia Capital, KAYAK, Tiger Global, Trinity Ventures, Sound Ventures and JLL. In December 2024 Life House combined its management portfolio with Lark Hotels to form Lark Hospitality — in which Lark holds the controlling interest — and spun its AI revenue-management platform out as Diamo. Life House never operated a public developer program: it was a consumer of hotel APIs (notably the Mews Open API) rather than a publisher of one, lifehousehotels.com now 301-redirects to larkhotels.com, no api/developer/docs subdomain resolves in DNS, and its GitHub organization holds a single fork of a third-party JavaScript library.

providers.name: Lo Que Necesito
providers.description: Lo Que Necesito (loquenecesito.co) is a Colombian real estate technology platform that lets people request and purchase housing online, accompanying customers through the buying process. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. A July 2026 enrichment pass found a live consumer website but no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Loose Cubes
providers.description: Loosecubes, Inc. was a membership-based marketplace often described as the "Airbnb for shared office space" — it connected people looking for a place to work with companies that had vacant desks and coworking space. Founded in 2010 in Brooklyn, New York by Campbell McKellar (Walmsley) and Anna Thomas, it raised roughly $9M total, including a $7.8M Series A led by New Enterprise Associates with Revolution Ventures and Battery Ventures participating. The company shut down and permanently closed in late 2012. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead; enrichment found no live API surface — the business is defunct and the loosecubes.com domain is now held by an unrelated owner.

providers.name: meetdavis
providers.description: Davis (meetdavis.com) is an AI-native real estate technology company, backed by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, that compresses early-stage real estate development from months to days. Davis combines proprietary AI models with human architect expertise to deliver feasibility studies (site analysis, regulatory diagnostics, volumetrics, financial modeling) and architectural designs (floor plans, unit-mix optimization, space planning) directly to developers and investors. Its first proprietary model, Gaudi-1, performs automated architectural generation under regulatory and financial constraints. Davis operates as a service model rather than selling software, and publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs at this time. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from the Balderton Capital portfolio and has been through the enrichment pipeline; no API surface was found.

providers.name: Modsy *
providers.description: Modsy was a consumer interior-design startup founded in 2015 offering online interior design with 3D room visualization technology. In 2022 it shifted away from consumer design services to focus on its core 3D home technology, and on August 30, 2023 its IP and team became part of Lennar to pursue the next generation of 3D innovation for the home. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer or API surface exists.

providers.name: Module
providers.description: Module is a vertically integrated sustainable housing company that designs, manufactures, and builds modular homes. Operating across design (architecture and engineering with BIM), manufacturing (its Last Mile Facility in Pittsburgh), and construction (licensed general contracting), Module focuses on infill and "missing middle" housing, small-footprint and energy-efficient affordable homes, and mixed-income developments through its Last Mile Network of design, construction, and mission-driven developer partner programs. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; Module publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Modus
providers.description: Modus (Modus Technologies, formerly Modus Closing) was a real estate closing, title, and escrow technology startup backed by 500 Global and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It built software to modernize the home-closing experience for buyers, sellers, and real estate agents. Modus was acquired by Compass in 2021; its standalone product was wound down and folded into Compass. As of this enrichment pass, modusclosing.com serves only a Compass-branded placeholder page (titled "Modus Technologies") that loads Compass CDN assets, and the company publishes no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs, SDKs, or any other public API surface. This profile is retained as an honest historical company record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Mosaic Building Group
providers.description: Mosaic (Mosaic Building Group) is a full-stack construction technology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. It is a national leader in build-to-rent residential construction and pre-development, pairing in-house software with local homebuilding partners to deliver personalized homes faster and at lower cost across Arizona and Texas. Its Mosaic Hub platform applies AI to construction planning and operations management. Backed by a16z (Series A lead) alongside Greylock, Innovation Endeavors, Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, SV Angel, and 8VC. Mosaic operates as a hybrid construction-plus-software business and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Mynd
providers.description: Mynd is a tech-enabled property management and real estate investing company offering full-service management for single-family rental (SFR) homes. It manages more than 20,000 homes across 40-plus U.S. markets, handling tenant screening, leasing, rent collection, maintenance, and portfolio management for individual and institutional investors, and provides a proprietary Investor Portal for real-time portfolio visibility. Mynd is owned by Roofstock and integrates with partner platforms such as Stessa. As of this enrichment pass Mynd publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile remains a company/portfolio lead with no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: MyNewPlace
providers.description: MyNewPlace is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: real-estate. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: nested
providers.description: Nested is a modern, technology-enabled UK estate agency that helps people sell, buy, and let residential property. It pairs hyper-local human agents with a digital platform and mobile app that give sellers transparency across the transaction, listing homes on major portals such as Rightmove, Zoopla, and OnTheMarket. Nested was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. The company operates a consumer-facing service and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation at this time.

providers.name: Noah
providers.description: Noah (originally founded as Patch Homes in 2016 and rebranded to Noah in 2020) was a US-based home-equity investment fintech backed by Union Square Ventures. It offered homeowners up-front financing in exchange for a share of their home's future appreciation, as an interest-free, no-monthly-payment alternative to a HELOC or cash-out refinance. The company raised roughly $156M across five rounds from seven investors before ceasing operations in 2024. This record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio lead; no live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Okol
providers.description: Okol operates propiedades.com, an online real estate marketplace serving Mexico where buyers and renters search residential and commercial property listings and connect with agents, developers, and brokers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, the company runs its consumer-facing listings platform on AWS but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specifications at this time.

providers.name: One Raven
providers.description: One Raven is a Phoenix, Arizona smart-home technology company building a local-first home automation platform designed for homeowners who want simplicity, privacy, and control. Its core product is the One Raven Home Server, which processes and stores home data locally rather than in the cloud, and ships pre-paired with a curated set of devices such as thermostats, smart locks, leak-detection and security sensors. The platform emphasizes local data storage, encrypted remote access, and a subscription-free model. Backed by a $5M seed round led by proptech investor Fifth Wall. One Raven does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Parkway Corp
providers.description: A Philadelphia-based real estate and parking infrastructure company that develops, owns, and manages parking facilities and mixed-use properties across the greater Philadelphia region. Parkway operates one of the largest privately held portfolios of urban parking and structured real estate assets in the Mid-Atlantic, providing on-street and off-street parking, monthly parking programs, validation services, and selective property development. The company does not publish a public developer API or partner integration portal.

providers.name: Pazpo
providers.description: Pazpo was an Indonesian property-technology (proptech) marketplace that billed itself as the country's first property search engine ("Mesin Pencari Properti Pertama di Indonesia"), letting users buy, sell, and rent homes, shophouses (ruko), apartments, warehouses, offices, and land across Jakarta, Tangerang, and the wider Indonesian market via web and a companion mobile app. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (500 Startups) and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for the enrichment pipeline. The enrichment pass found the company defunct: the pazpo.id domain no longer resolves (DNS lookup fails), and by 2024 the lapsed domain had been taken over by an unrelated Indonesian online-gambling ("togel") site. No live website, developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists to harvest; historical detail here is reconstructed from Internet Archive captures (2015-2017).

providers.name: PeerStreet
providers.description: PeerStreet was a two-sided marketplace for real estate debt investing that connected individual and institutional investors with short-term, high-yield real estate loans originated by a nationwide network of private lenders. The platform let investors build diversified portfolios of loan positions, earn monthly interest, and access loan-level documentation and performance data, along with a "Pocket" cash account and self-directed IRA options for accredited investors. Operating as a licensed California finance lender (License 60DBO-45398) and backed by a16z, PeerStreet transacted more than $5B across 47 states before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2023. The company is profiled in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: PictureWorks
providers.description: PictureWorks (PictureWorks Technology) was a digital imaging technology company based in Danville, California that built imaging tools and services for the real estate and e-commerce industries, enabling online visual presentation of products and properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. The company was acquired by Internet Pictures Corporation (IPIX) in 2000. No public developer API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or SDK surface could be located for this entity during enrichment; the active pictureworks.com (Pictureworks Group, Singapore theme-park imaging) is a separate, unrelated company and is not linked here to avoid mis-attribution.

providers.name: Pinhome
providers.description: Pinhome is an Indonesian proptech real estate marketplace for smart buying, selling, and renting of houses, apartments, offices, and shop-houses (Pintar Jual Beli Sewa Rumah). The platform spans property listings and search, mortgage (KPR) and loan-takeover facilitation with partner banks, an automated property valuation tool (Pinvalue), and a marketplace of household and property services. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Pinhome operates a consumer-facing web and mobile product and does not publish a public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Plan0 Ai
providers.description: Plan0 AI is a real estate construction technology company that applies AI to preconstruction cost estimation and design analysis. Its platform turns architectural drawings into detailed cost estimates and 3D models in roughly 30 minutes rather than the traditional two-week cycle, and adds automated takeoff and pricing, value-engineering scenario simulation, and predictive analytics. Plan0 AI serves real estate developers underwriting and making preconstruction design decisions, general contractors producing business- development estimates and cost forecasts, and investors validating pro-formas and benchmarking. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and demo-booking website only, with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: playhouse
providers.description: Playhouse is a consumer real estate application that combines homes-for-sale listings with community polls and reactions. Home searchers, neighbors, homebuyers, investors, and real estate professionals browse luxury and residential listings and react to them, turning property discovery into a social, opinion-driven experience. The product ships as native iOS and Android apps backed by a private api.playhouse.so service; there is no publicly documented developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or API reference surface. Playhouse is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile was enriched from live probes of its Webflow marketing site, app-store listings, and DNS/TLS records.

providers.name: Porch
providers.description: Porch Group is a home services and home insurance platform operating across the full lifecycle of the home. Trading on Nasdaq as PRCH, the company combines a vertical software business for home inspectors, moving companies, title and mortgage providers, and contractors with a consumer-facing home insurance carrier (Porch Insurance Reciprocal Exchange), home warranty, and a moving-concierge app that helps homeowners set up utilities, security, and services. Porch reaches a large share of U.S. homebuyers each year through its inspection-software network, using that unique early-in-the-home-lifecycle data to power insurance, warranty, and moving offerings. This profile was seeded as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Porch publishes no public developer API, but it does operate a responsible disclosure program and RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Portal Terreno
providers.description: Portal Terreno is an online marketplace for land and parcels ("terrenos" and "parcelas") in Latin America, operating localized classifieds portals for Chile (portalterreno.cl) and Mexico (portalterreno.com.mx) with tens of thousands of land listings. The Next.js web platform lets buyers search, filter, and contact sellers to find land for sale, while sellers and real-estate agents publish listings. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer, API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found during the enrichment pass; the domain-security posture was probed live.

providers.name: PulteGroup
providers.description: PulteGroup is one of America's largest homebuilding companies, building homes under the Centex, Pulte Homes, Del Webb, DiVosta Homes, John Wieland Homes, and American West brands. No public developer APIs have been identified at this time; this index tracks the company's public web properties.

providers.name: rentify
providers.description: Rentify was a London-based property technology (PropTech) startup founded in 2011 that built an online lettings and property-management platform for landlords, letting them list, market, price, and manage rental properties directly without a traditional high-street agent. It raised a Series A from Balderton Capital and later a crowdfunding round before ceasing operations. Surfaced as a balderton-capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface (the company is no longer operating and rentify.com no longer serves an application).

providers.name: Rentlytics
providers.description: Rentlytics was a multifamily real estate data analytics company founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, CA (with offices in Sacramento and Denver). Its platform consolidated operational and financial data scattered across multifamily assets into a unified business-intelligence layer, and it shipped products such as Open Data Services and Renovation Manager for per-unit and per-property yield visibility. Rentlytics was acquired by RealPage in 2018 for roughly $57 million and folded into RealPage's real-estate platform. As of this enrichment pass the standalone rentlytics.com domain is parked (it redirects to a generic lander) and the company operates no independent public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: RentMineOnline
providers.description: RentMineOnline was a San Francisco-based software-as-a-service company, founded in 2007, that brought resident referral programs online for the multifamily rental housing industry by leveraging leading social networking sites. Its platform sent community-branded emails to apartment residents and paid them referral bonuses for recommending their buildings to friends across their social networks. In 2011 it was voted "Best New Company in Apartment Marketing." RentMineOnline was acquired by RealPage in July 2012 and folded into RealPage's multifamily marketing portfolio; it no longer operates an independent website or developer program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this profile was processed by the enrichment pipeline, which confirmed no public API surface, developer documentation, or discovery artifacts exist for the defunct entity.

providers.name: Revolution Precrafted
providers.description: Revolution Precrafted is a Manila, Philippines-based prefabricated design and proptech company founded in 2015 by Robbie Antonio. It designs and sells limited-edition prefab homes, pavilions, modular hotels, pop-up retail spaces, glamping structures, and furniture created by more than 80 leading global architects, designers, and artists under exclusive partnership. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Durians) and K2 Global, it reached a reported unicorn valuation. The company runs a consumer real-estate and construction business and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and mislabeled "Strategic Grow" in the source stub; the website revolutionprecrafted.com is authoritative.

providers.name: Samara
providers.description: Samara is a residential design and construction company that builds prefabricated, factory-made homes. Founded as an independent venture by Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia, Samara designs and delivers backyard accessory dwelling units (ADUs) in configurable Studio, One Bedroom, Two Bedroom, XL 8 and XL 10 models, alongside "Locale by Samara" single-family homes and a modular "kit of parts" for higher-yield multifamily infill. The company pairs a consumer-facing online configurator, property-eligibility checks, financing options and regional showrooms with factory production and installation. Backed by General Catalyst, Samara operates in the housing, construction technology and real-estate space. It is a physical-product company with no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Silagroup
providers.description: SILA is a next-generation business services and real estate platform based in India, backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It delivers strategic solutions across Facility Management, Material Handling Services, Food & Catering, Real Estate Advisory, and Real Estate Development, supporting corporate entities, real estate funds, landowners, and developers throughout the entire real estate lifecycle. SILA runs a WordPress-based corporate website (silagroup.co.in) and publishes no public developer API surface; the only exposed HTTP API is the internal WordPress REST (wp-json) endpoint used to render the CMS. Enrichment confirmed no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, no /.well-known discovery documents, and no developer portal, SDKs, or docs as of this pass.

providers.name: Spacemaker
providers.description: Spacemaker was a Norwegian proptech startup (founded 2016 in Oslo) that built cloud-based, AI-assisted generative design software for early-stage real estate and urban site planning, letting architects, developers, and urban planners rapidly explore massing, sunlight, wind, noise, and view analyses to optimize buildable sites. Backed by investors including Northzone, Spacemaker was acquired by Autodesk in November 2020 (reported ~$240M) and its technology was continued and rebranded as Autodesk Forma. The standalone spacemaker.ai domain now permanently (301) redirects to the Autodesk Forma product page, so there is no longer an independent Spacemaker developer portal, API, or documentation surface; developer/API access is provided through Autodesk Forma and the broader Autodesk Platform Services ecosystem.

providers.name: SpeedHome
providers.description: SpeedHome is a Malaysian online property rental marketplace that connects landlords and tenants directly, best known for its zero-deposit rental model backed by tenancy protection. The platform covers listing, tenant screening, digital tenancy agreements, rent collection, and landlord protection through its consumer-facing web and mobile applications. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Sumutasu
providers.description: Sumutasu Inc. (株式会社すむたす) is a Japanese property-technology (proptech) company operating under the mission "a society where people can make ideal housing choices" (住まいの理想的な選択ができる社会に). It runs an instant real-estate buying and selling service for used condominiums in Japan, using data and technology to give homeowners a fast, transparent alternative to the traditional brokerage process, alongside an agent-assisted sales offering. The company is backed by 500 Global. Its public presence is a corporate marketing website (About, Services, Members, News, and Careers) built on the Studio.Design no-code platform; no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface has been found.

providers.name: View The Space (Fmr Hightower)
providers.description: VTS (View The Space, formed in part from the Hightower merger) is a commercial real estate technology platform for leasing, asset management, tenant experience, and market analytics used by landlords, brokers, and property managers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Probing found the marketing site (www.vts.com) behind a bot challenge and a bare backend host (api.vts.com) with no publicly documented API program, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this remains a company profile rather than a documented API.

providers.name: VivaReal
providers.description: VivaReal operates vivareal.com.br, a Brazilian online real estate marketplace and classifieds portal where consumers search, buy, sell, and rent residential and commercial properties across Brazil, connecting property seekers with real estate agents, agencies, and developers. It was originally backed by 500 Global and later became part of Grupo ZAP / OLX Brasil. It was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; an enrichment pass found no public developer API surface, portal, or specification.

providers.name: Zeus
providers.description: Zeus (Zeus Living) was a furnished and corporate housing rental startup founded by Kulveer Taggar (previously co-founder of Auctomatic with Patrick Collison). The company leased and managed furnished residences that it re-let to business travelers, relocating employees, and companies needing flexible medium-term housing, backed by investors including Bloomberg Beta. Zeus Living has since wound down operations; its zeusliving.com domain no longer resolves and it exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile was surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed no live API or web presence remains.

providers.name: ZipMatch
providers.description: ZipMatch was an online real estate marketplace and property portal based in the Philippines, backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) among other investors, that helped buyers and renters discover homes, condominiums, and other property listings across Metro Manila and the wider Philippine market. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears to be defunct: the zipmatch.com domain is still registered (GoDaddy, registry expiry 2029) but has no DNS delegation — no NS, A, MX, or TXT records resolve — so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; no API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Ziroom
providers.description: Ziroom (自如) is a Beijing-based proptech company operating China's largest centralized long-term apartment rental platform. Spun out of the Lianjia (Homelink) real-estate group in 2011, it leases, renovates, furnishes and manages residential units and re-rents them to urban tenants through its app and website, layering on cleaning, maintenance and smart-home services. It is backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund, Tencent and Sequoia Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment found no publicly discoverable developer or API surface.

providers.name: Hosta a.i.
providers.description: Hosta a.i. is an AI-powered remote property assessment platform that turns ordinary photographs from any camera into precise measurements, detailed floor plans, material classifications, condition assessments, and bills of materials. Using patented AI spatial and material analytics, Hosta automates onsite property analysis without specialized equipment or site visits, and exposes these capabilities through configurable APIs so insurers, appraisers, inspectors, contractors, property managers, home-improvement platforms, and furniture retailers can embed remote assessment into their existing workflows and systems. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Hosta is a Techstars- and Eclipse-backed company operating on a secure AWS cloud platform with PII filtering protections.

providers.name: Leap To Win Technologies Private
providers.description: Leap To Win Technologies Private Limited is a Bengaluru, India company incorporated on 26 June 2024 (CIN U62090KA2024PTC190203) that operates Propico (propico.in), a rental guarantee and property management service. For property owners Propico underwrites a fixed guaranteed monthly rent with zero-vacancy risk, handling tenant screening and placement, rent collection, inspections, maintenance coordination and legal compliance; for tenants it sells rental protection plans covering unfair security-deposit deductions and surprise move-out costs. The company markets two packages - a Premium Guaranteed plan and a Standard property-management plan - and serves Bangalore, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Delhi NCR and Pune. Propico runs a marketing and customer web app backed by an authenticated multi-service API gateway at api.propico.in, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or OpenAPI definition. It does publish a well-formed llms.txt, making it agent-discoverable as a content surface even though it exposes no programmable interface.

providers.name: Rithm Capital
providers.description: Rithm Capital is a global asset manager focused on real estate, credit, and financial services.
