Through subsidiaries such as Newrez, Genesis Capital, Sculptor Capital Management, and Adoor, Rithm operates across mortgage origination and servicing, single-family rental, business-purpose lending, and alternative investment strategies. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified at the parent company level.

providers.name: VICI Properties
providers.description: VICI Properties is an experiential real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns one of the largest portfolios of gaming, hospitality, and entertainment destinations in the United States, including Caesars Palace and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas. The company holds long-term triple-net leases with leading gaming operators. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified; VICI engages investors and partners through corporate and investor relations channels.

providers.name: Green Canopy NODE
providers.description: Green Canopy NODE is a Seattle- and Portland-based sustainable real estate development and construction technology company that designs and builds all-electric, low-carbon homes. The business operates across three lines: prefabricated "Building Kits" (including mass-timber panelized systems), full development services for multi-unit and infill housing projects, and impact investment funds that finance green housing. The company reports 300+ all-electric homes built, five real estate investment funds, and roughly 35K metric tons of greenhouse-gas emissions mitigated since inception. Green Canopy NODE was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a marketing and investor website but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Brace
providers.description: Brace (Brace Software, Inc., brace.ai) was a Culver City, California fintech founded in 2017 by Eric Rachmel and Amr Mohamed that rebuilt mortgage default servicing as software. Its Default Management Platform covered the end-to-end loss-mitigation lifecycle for servicers, lenders and investors — a homeowner engagement portal, a centralized responsive application, a rules and underwriting engine, document classification and data extraction, and event-driven communications and reporting — replacing the paper-based, inconsistent default workflows used by top U.S. mortgage servicers. The company raised a reported ~$30M and was acquired by Boston-based mortgage technology firm Stavvy, announced 1 August 2023, folding Brace's loss-mitigation platform into Stavvy's eClosing, digital notarization and foreclosure suite. Brace does not survive as an independent surface: brace.ai now 301-redirects every path to stavvy.com/mortgage-servicing-solution, and no docs., developer., api. or app. subdomain resolves in DNS. No public API, developer portal, machine-readable specification or SDK was ever published under the Brace brand — the Wayback CDX index for brace.ai carries no developer or API path — so this profile records identity and exit rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Domio
providers.description: Domio was a New York City hospitality and real-estate technology company that designed, leased, and operated branded "apart-hotels" — spacious, design-forward apartment-style accommodations aimed at group and extended-stay travelers. Founded in June 2016 by former Bank of America Merrill Lynch real-estate bankers Jay Roberts and Adrian Lam, the company used data analysis and machine learning to select buildings for its portfolio and distributed inventory through its own site and app alongside third-party channels such as Airbnb. It raised roughly $117M across five rounds, including a $12M Series A in 2018 from Tribeca Venture Partners and SoftBank Capital, a $50M joint-venture facility from Upper90, and a $100M Series B in December 2019 (half equity, half debt) led by GGV Capital with Eldridge Industries, 3L Capital, Cain International and Tenaya Capital. Airbnb suspended all of Domio's host accounts in August 2020, the co-founders resigned that September, and the company ceased operations in November 2020, selling its assets through an assignment for the benefit of creditors overseen by Sherwood Partners. Domio never published a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification. Its former host staydomio.com was re-registered on 2021-09-19 by an unrelated party and now serves a GoDaddy parking lander, so it is deliberately not wired as a Website pointer. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: EasyKnock
providers.description: EasyKnock was a New York based residential real estate fintech, founded in 2016 by Jared Kessler, that pioneered consumer sale-leaseback in the United States: homeowners sold their house to EasyKnock for cash and stayed on as renting tenants with an option to repurchase. The company raised roughly $430 million in equity and debt and rolled up several proptech businesses — Ribbon Home, Onder, Balance Home, HomePace and FarmlandFinder — before consumer lawsuits and state attorney general and regulator actions in Massachusetts, Michigan, Connecticut, Texas, Maryland, South Carolina, Pennsylvania and Ohio over its sale-leaseback disclosures. EasyKnock announced it had closed its doors on December 6, 2024. Its website is now a single static shutdown notice, its api.easyknock.com host answers Cloudflare error 1016 (origin DNS deleted), and it never published a public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Prescient
providers.description: Prescient Co. Inc. was a United States construction-technology and manufacturing company that sold an integrated design, engineering, manufacturing and assembly platform for multi-unit buildings — apartments, condominiums, student and military dormitories, hotels and senior-living communities. Its product was the patented Prescient Solution built on the Unified Truss Construction System (UTCS), a light-gauge steel structural framing system manufactured off-site in panelised components and assembled on-site, marketed as a faster, greener and lower-cost alternative to conventional cast-in-place and wood-frame structures at heights up to roughly twelve stories. The "technology" in the offering was internal design-automation software that linked architectural design, structural engineering, factory manufacturing and field assembly into one digital model; it was delivered as a design-build service to real-estate developers and general contractors, never as a product a third party could integrate with. Founded in 2012 (some sources list 2013) and headquartered in North Carolina — Charlotte, later Durham — with manufacturing in Mebane, North Carolina and Arvada, Colorado, the company raised a large private round stack including a $40M Series D and a Series E led by Eldridge Industries at a reported $650M valuation; publicly reported lifetime totals disagree, with EquityZen listing $103M and Crunchbase reporting roughly $375M through Series G. The company contracted sharply: the Mebane plant closed in 2022 with 83 jobs cut, 50 Arvada jobs were cut in April 2023, and a Colorado WARN notice filed on 31 August 2023 announced the permanent closure of the Arvada plant and a further 60 jobs, stating that upon conclusion of the shutdown activities the company would be closed. Prescient never operated a public developer program, API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification, and prescientco.com has since passed out of the company's control. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Stay Alfred
providers.description: Stay Alfred Inc. was a Spokane, Washington short-term-rental and hospitality operator that pioneered the "travel apartment" — full apartments in walkable downtown cores, leased in bulk from multifamily building owners and operated with hotel-style consistency, cleaning and guest support. Founded in 2011 by Jordan Allen, who was named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year for the Pacific Northwest in 2019, the company grew to roughly 2,000-2,500 units across 28 to 33 U.S. markets including Denver, San Diego, Miami, New Orleans and Nashville, hosted around half a million guests, and employed more than 230 people. It raised approximately $62M in total venture funding, headlined by a $47M Series B in October 2018 led by Chicago real-estate technology fund Nine Four Ventures. Distribution ran through its own consumer booking site and the major online travel agencies, so Stay Alfred was an API CONSUMER rather than an API publisher; it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification. COVID-19 ended it: the company closed every property nationwide from 1 April 2020, a rescue funding round was withdrawn at the last minute, and on 20 May 2020 Stay Alfred announced it would close permanently, winding down through mid-2020 while it had been on track for roughly $100M in revenue that year. The stayalfred.com domain is still on its original 2013 registration but is no longer controlled by the company: it is privacy-shielded, Cloudflare-hosted, and every path now 301-redirects into a rotating chain of unrelated third-party sites. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Uptime
providers.description: Uptime (Uptime SAS, Paris, SIREN 822006839) was a French elevator predictive-maintenance company founded in 2016 by Augustin and Amaury Celier. It fitted 4G-connected sensors to existing elevators and used the resulting telemetry to predict failures, dispatch technicians and report availability to building managers, backed by Serena and angels including Jacques-Antoine Granjon, David Amsellem, Yvan Wibaux and Antoine Martin across roughly EUR 10M of funding. The Paris Commercial Court opened a redressement judiciaire on 2022-07-26 and pronounced liquidation judiciaire with a plan de cession to SAS Otis on 2022-10-20; the elevator-maintenance activity and a minority of staff transferred to Otis. The company never published a public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification, and the uptime.ac domain has since lapsed — it now 301-redirects every path to unrelated third-party sites. This profile is retained as an honest record of a defunct company with no API surface.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: Gaming and Leisure Properties
providers.description: Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc. (NASDAQ: GLPI) is "the nation's first real estate investment trust focused on acquiring real property assets leased to gaming operators." Headquartered in Wyomissing, Pennsylvania, GLPI's portfolio comprises 71 premier gaming and related facilities across 21 states, totaling more than 29.3 million square feet and over 15,100 hotel rooms, leased on a triple-net basis to operators including Penn Entertainment, Caesars Entertainment, Bally's Corporation, Boyd Gaming, the Cordish Companies, and Hard Rock. No public developer API, data feed, or GitHub organization has been identified; GLPI engages investors, tenants, and partners through corporate and investor relations channels only.

providers.name: Sun Communities
providers.description: Sun Communities, Inc. is a real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns, operates, and develops manufactured home communities, recreational vehicle resorts, and marinas across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The company is one of the largest operators in its sector and is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: Tri Pointe Homes
providers.description: Tri Pointe Homes is one of the largest homebuilders in the United States, designing and constructing premium single-family detached and attached homes across multiple regional markets. The company also offers in-house mortgage, title, and insurance services through its Tri Pointe Connect affiliates. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified; the company engages homebuyers and broker partners through its consumer website and broker program.

providers.name: Vestris
providers.description: Vestris is an AI-powered platform that automates the real estate pre-closing process for mortgage title and closing operations. It uses browser agents to log into county tax portals, extract property records, parse purchase contracts, run tax calculations, generate title abstracts, and produce title commitments and closing documents. Positioned as "the AI processing unit for mortgage title and closing," Vestris aims to replace manual title searchers and accelerate property deal closing. The company is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup based in San Francisco. As of this profile it operates a product application (waitlist / demo access) with no publicly documented developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Ajar Online
providers.description: Ajar Online is a cloud-based property management and rent-collection platform headquartered in Kuwait and founded in 2015. It lets landlords, real-estate agencies, and property managers digitize rent collection and property administration, sending payment requests to tenants over SMS and email and accepting payment via credit and debit cards, KNET, and Sadad so tenants can pay in under a minute from anywhere. The platform adds portfolio dashboards, tenant and contract management, and analytics for data-driven property decisions, and has expanded across the GCC into the UAE and Saudi Arabia. The company operates a live, authenticated API backend at api.joinajar.com; there is no public API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or SDK published at this time, so this profile captures verifiable identity and domain-security signals pending a public developer surface.

providers.name: D.R. Horton
providers.description: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder by volume in the United States, building and selling single-family homes in dozens of states across multiple price points. The company is a Fortune 500 enterprise with affiliated financial services including DHI Mortgage, DHI Title, and DRH Insurance.

providers.name: Dream Finders Homes

Rocket Companies does not publish a public corporate developer API portal at the holding-company level.

providers.name: Extra Space Storage
providers.description: Extra Space Storage Inc. is a fully integrated, self-administered and self-managed real estate investment trust (REIT) and one of the largest operators of self-storage properties in the United States. The company owns, operates, and manages thousands of self-storage facilities across the country, offering storage units, vehicle storage, and business storage solutions. Extra Space Storage does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: Saul Ewing LLP
providers.description: Saul Ewing LLP is a U.S.-based law firm founded in 1921 as Saul, Ewing, Remick & Saul, with more than 450 attorneys across 17 U.S. offices spanning the Mid-Atlantic, Northeast, Midwest, Florida, and California. The firm serves clients across 40+ industries with practice strengths in litigation, corporate and M&A, bankruptcy and restructuring, real estate, public finance, life sciences, financial services, intellectual property, labor and employment, and cybersecurity and privacy. Saul Ewing does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or machine-readable data product; its public technology surface is limited to its corporate website, a HighQ-powered client portal, the SEquel Alumni Portal at alumni.saul.com, employee remote-access tooling, and a small set of practice-specific blogs (Construction Industry Counselor, OZ and EB-5 Investments, Legacy Matters, The Friday Five). Two empty GitHub organizations (Saul-Ewing and saulewing) exist with zero public repositories.

providers.name: Cozen O'Connor
providers.description: Cozen O'Connor is a full-service U.S. law firm founded in 1970 and headquartered in Philadelphia, with more than 1,000 attorneys across 33+ offices in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The firm is ranked among the top 100 law firms in America and is best known for its nationally recognized subrogation, insurance, labor and employment, global corporate, intellectual property, and government relations practices. Cozen O'Connor Public Strategies, the firm's bipartisan federal, state, and local government affairs and lobbying arm, operates from Washington, D.C. and major state capitals. The firm operates an unusually broad thought-leadership network of LexBlog/WordPress-powered blogs and podcasts (subrogation, cyber law, health law, state AGs, transformative AI, OSHA, employment law, family law, property insurance, casualty coverage, real estate / land use, professional responsibility, and a Public Strategies feed), each of which exposes a standard `/feed/` RSS endpoint. Cozen O'Connor does not operate a public developer program, REST/GraphQL API, SDK ecosystem, or GitHub organization. This profile catalogs the firm's public-facing knowledge surface — practice and industry pages, attorney directory, ancillary businesses, lobbying arm, and the blog/podcast RSS network — rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Sidekick Data
providers.description: Sidekick is a professional AI assistant for real estate agents and brokerages, built on the same large language model technology that powers ChatGPT with custom integrations into real estate-specific data sources. From a chat-style interface it combines an agent's inputs with MLS data feeds, local market insights, and a brokerage's brand preferences to produce detailed, on-voice outputs - covering client relationship tracking, email and call interaction analysis, market trend monitoring, property comparisons, transaction document management, and compliance risk detection. Sidekick is directly integrated with MLS and association data feeds across the United States and is backed by investors including Socium Ventures, Swift Ventures, and Garuda Ventures. It is a consumer/professional SaaS product and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Buildscience
providers.description: BuildScience Inc. (Y Combinator Winter 2015) was a PropTech startup based in Mountain View, California that built an operating-system platform for commercial buildings. Its software let building owners and facility operators deploy customized building-management solutions intended to reduce operational costs while improving tenant satisfaction, and the company reported deploying in a one-million-square-foot Class A office building. As of the 2026 enrichment pass the company appears dormant: the buildscience.com domain no longer serves a live product (the host returns a CloudFront default certificate that does not match the domain and a broken origin), no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be located, and the organization's single public GitHub repository was last updated in January 2020. This profile is retained as a verified-identity network record; no API artifacts could be enriched because the provider publishes no live API.

providers.name: Realtor.com
providers.description: Realtor.com is a real estate listings website operated by Move, Inc., a subsidiary of News Corp, headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The platform is the official site of the National Association of REALTORS (NAR) under a long-term operating agreement and is one of the largest U.S. property search portals, serving home buyers, sellers, renters, and real estate professionals. Realtor.com aggregates for-sale, for-rent, and off-market listings sourced primarily from Multiple Listing Services (MLSs) via Move's listings distribution subsidiary ListHub, and surfaces them through consumer web and mobile apps alongside neighborhood, school, mortgage, and market data. The professional side of the business sells lead-generation and marketing products such as Connections Plus, ReadyConnect Concierge, and Market VIP to agents and brokers, while ListHub provides MLS-to-portal syndication, broker reporting, and listing feed management. Adjacent Move properties include Doorsteps, Moving.com, and SeniorHousingNet, and the company publishes a public economic research arm at realtor.com/research that releases monthly housing market reports and downloadable historical datasets. Realtor.com does not publish a first-party public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; programmatic access to listing data is gated through MLS membership and ListHub's broker/vendor agreements, while the only widely available HTTP APIs branded as Realtor.com are unofficial third-party scrapers hosted on RapidAPI and Apify.

providers.name: Fidelity National Financial
providers.description: Fidelity National Financial (FNF) is a leading provider of title insurance, escrow, and other title-related services, as well as transaction services to the real estate and mortgage industries. FNF also operates F&G Annuities & Life and owns technology providers including SoftPro and ServiceLink that serve the title, real estate, and mortgage workflow.

providers.name: simplifile
providers.description: Simplifile is a real estate document collaboration and electronic recording (e-recording) network that connects settlement agents, lenders, and county recording offices to submit, track, and record property documents electronically. Its platform also covers post-closing collaboration, lien release, and trailing-document management for the mortgage and title industry. Simplifile is part of ICE Mortgage Technology (Intercontinental Exchange). This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched via live domain and endpoint probing; no public developer API surface was found.

providers.name: Primus Senior Living
providers.description: Primus Senior Living is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of general-catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Unreal Estate
providers.description: Unreal Estate (formerly USRealty.com) is a tech-enabled flat-fee real estate marketplace and brokerage that lets home sellers list on their local MLS without paying a traditional listing commission, with flat-fee plans ranging from $0 to $449 upfront plus 0.5% at closing, available nationwide except South Dakota. The company also offers buyer services, rental listings with cash rebates, and AI-powered market intelligence, and was acquired by Abode in November 2024. Unreal Estate publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Ballard Spahr
providers.description: Ballard Spahr LLP is a national U.S. law firm founded in 1885 and headquartered in Philadelphia. Following its January 1, 2025 combination with Seattle-based Lane Powell, the firm operates as a "nationally recognized firm of more than 750 lawyers across 18 U.S. offices" with departments in Business and Transactions, Finance, Intellectual Property, Litigation, and Real Estate. The firm has historic depth in consumer financial services, real estate, public finance, and IP, and runs widely read thought-leadership properties including the Consumer Finance Monitor blog (with public RSS feed) and the Business Better podcast. Ballard Spahr does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is the Consumer Finance Monitor RSS feed.

providers.name: Realogy Holdings
providers.description: Realogy Holdings (now Anywhere Real Estate) is a global provider of residential real estate services with brands including Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate, Century 21, Coldwell Banker, Corcoran, ERA, and Sotheby's International Realty. Realogy Holdings does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integrations are managed through brand-specific technology platforms and partner programs.

providers.name: Moveha
providers.description: Moveha is a student-housing and long-term rental platform for the United States, built to help college students and relocating professionals find, reserve, and secure off-campus housing before they arrive in the country. Founded by former international students and backed by 500 Global, Moveha positions itself as an "Airbnb for long-term rentals" — a faster, more transparent way to browse verified properties, reserve remotely, share rooms, or list a property for lease, with identity-verified users. As of this enrichment pass Moveha publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Dechert
providers.description: Dechert LLP is a global law firm founded in 1875 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with "more than 900 lawyers" across 22 offices in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia (Wikipedia cites roughly 1,000 attorneys in 20 offices; the firm itself emphasizes a global footprint spanning the U.S., Europe, Asia, and the Middle East). The firm is known for market-leading practices in financial services and investment management, private equity, private credit, mergers and acquisitions, international arbitration, intellectual property, life sciences, white collar enforcement, and antitrust. Dechert publishes deep thought-leadership through its OnPoint series, Crypto Bytes, FSR Radar, THE CRED, and ReTorts; produces multiple podcasts (Dechert 4 Real, Committed Capital, Dechert On Reg); and operates proprietary information platforms including DAMITT (Dechert Antitrust Merger Investigation Timing Tracker), World Compass, World Passport, Dechert Direct, and a Box Portal. Despite these data-driven products, Dechert does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GraphQL endpoint, webhook surface, status page, changelog, or developer portal, and does not publish an RSS feed for OnPoint or any blog series — its only public-facing subscription mechanism is an email preference form.

providers.name: Dora
providers.description: Dora (Hola Dora) is a Colombian proptech and fintech startup, founded in 2023 and headquartered in Bogota, that acts as a rental guarantee for the residential real-estate market. It underwrites tenants in roughly five minutes over WhatsApp with no guarantor or co-signer, generates a digitally signed lease, and then guarantees the rent to landlords and property managers by paying the monthly amount on a fixed day whether or not the tenant has paid. Its InvestigaDora, ContrataDora and GarantizaDora flows cover tenant screening, electronic contracting, and guaranteed collection, reconciliation and payout for real-estate operators.

providers.name: Flex
providers.description: Flex is a consumer financial technology company that lets renters pay their monthly rent in smaller installments spread across the month, instead of a single lump sum on the due date, so payments better fit each person's pay schedule and cash flow. The company pays the landlord or property manager in full on the due date and collects from the renter over the month, positioning itself as a flexible-payments layer on top of the largest recurring expense most households carry. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York City, Flex operates a consumer mobile app and partners with property-management platforms; it is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and surfaced in the 500 Global portfolio. Flex publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or discovery surface today - this profile is a network lead.

providers.name: StreamLoan
providers.description: StreamLoan was a digital mortgage software company offering a point-of-sale (POS) and loan-origination platform that connected loan officers, borrowers, and real-estate agents to convert leads into funded home loans faster. Its toolkit spanned lead management, borrower communication and collaboration, workflow automation, document collection, security/privacy controls, and a branded borrower experience aimed at cutting the 40+ day mortgage close cycle. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - streamloan.io is parked on a registrar IP and every developer/app/api/docs/portal subdomain is unreachable (DNS records remain but no host responds), and no public API or developer program was ever documented.

providers.name: mcmakler
providers.description: McMakler is a German hybrid residential real-estate brokerage (proptech) headquartered in Berlin, combining local human agents with in-house technology to list, market, and sell homes across Germany, Austria, and France. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 probed the public surface and found no public developer API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known discovery catalog; an internal backend host (api.mcmakler.de) exists but returns 403 and is not a published API. Domain transport/email security was probed and recorded.

providers.name: Loftium
providers.description: Loftium was a Seattle-based real-estate technology startup (founded 2017) that helped renters and aspiring homebuyers cover a down payment by hosting a room or unit on Airbnb and sharing the short-term rental income. It later pivoted to a rent-to-own model. Loftium was acquired by Flyhomes in February 2023. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of threshold-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment pass (2026-07-20) found no public API, developer portal, or documentation: the loftium.com domain no longer serves company content and 301-redirects to unrelated parked domains, and no api/docs/developer subdomains resolve. No API surface exists to catalog.
